  Build pipeline for this manuscript (first draft, 2026-11-06)

  relative to the repository root. Origin of the prose: paper 02's
  report.Rmd at commit c866404be (sections sec-comparators,
  sec-pathways, sec-alternatives, sec-prognostic, sec-trend,
  sec-random, "What the expectancy terms are for", and the matching

```{r values-provenance, include = FALSE}
pub_metas <- list(stress = st_p_m, gapC = gfC_m, blkT = rvT_m,
                  blkN = rvN_m, blkA = rvA_m, tier1 = s27_m,
                  scen = s21_m)
pub_metas <- pub_metas[!vapply(pub_metas, is.null, logical(1))]
claim(all(vapply(pub_metas, pub_ok, logical(1))),
      'Every published-set run records param_set = published.')
if (!is.na(sigma_br)) {
  setv('sig_br', sprintf('%g', sigma_br))
  setv('sig_pb', sprintf('%g', sigma_pb))
  setv('truth45', fs2(-0.45 * sigma_br))
  setv('truth30', fs2(-0.30 * sigma_br))
}
if (!is.na(sigma_pb_simcore)) {
  setv('sig_pb_sc', sprintf('%g', sigma_pb_simcore))
  claim(sigma_pb > sigma_pb_simcore,
        'The published placebo-response SD exceeds the simcore2026 SD.')
}
```

```{r values-ceil, include = FALSE}
if (has_ceil) {
  cr <- ceil$results
  bnd <- function(cp, g) cr$ceiling[cr$coupling == cp & cr$given == g]
  setv('b_bm', f3(bnd('c_bm', 'alone')))
  setv('b_pb', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'alone')))
  setv('b_pb30', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.3')))
  setv('b_pb45', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45')))
  setv('b_bl30', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3')))
  setv('b_bl45', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.45')))
  claim(is.na(bnd('c_bm', 'c_pb = 0.6')) &&
          is.na(bnd('c_bm', 'c_tv = 0.6')),
        'No c_bm is feasible with c_pb or c_tv at 0.6.')
  claim(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45') > 0.3,
        'Strength 0.3 lies inside the bound at c_bm = 0.45.')
}
```

```{r values-stress, include = FALSE}
if (has_st_p) {
  n_st <- st_p_m$n_reps
  setv('st_n', fn(n_st))
  setv('st_band', band_txt(n_st))
  s3n <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0, pathway != 'progtvgrow')
  g9n <- s3n |> filter(method == 'E7cr2')
  g10n <- s3n |> filter(method == 'E7null_cr2')
  fbn <- s3n |> filter(method == 'F1A0B')
  setv('st_g9_null', rng(g9n$reject))
  setv('st_g10_null', rng(g10n$reject))
  setv('st_fb_null', rng(fbn$reject))
  claim(all(in_band(g9n$reject, n_st)),
        'Stress job: G9 null inside the band at strength 0.3.')
  claim(all(in_band(g10n$reject, n_st)),
        'Stress job: G10 null inside the band at strength 0.3.')
  pw <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0.45,
           method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1A0B')) |>
    select(pathway, N, method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = reject)
  setv('st_g9_alt', rng(pw$E7cr2))
  setv('st_fb_g10', rng(pw$F1A0B - pw$E7null_cr2, fs3))
  tvg <- st_p |>
    filter(pathway == 'progtvgrow') |>
    select(c_bm, N, method, strength, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = strength, values_from = reject,
                names_prefix = 's')
  claim(isTRUE(all.equal(tvg$s0.3, tvg$s0.6)),
        'Constant shift: identical rejection at both strengths.')
  cells <- st_p |>
    group_by(cell_id, pathway, strength, c_bm, N) |>
    summarise(nmax = max(n, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  six <- cells |> filter(strength == 0.6, pathway != 'progtvgrow')
  setv('n6_cells', nrow(six))
  setv('n6_refused', sum(six$nmax == 0))
  refused <- six |> filter(nmax == 0)
  setv('n6_ran', sum(six$nmax > 0))
  if (has_pdc) {
    rep_cfg <- pdc$summary |>
      filter(paths_repaired > 0) |>
      transmute(key = paste(pathway, strength, c_bm))
    ref_cfg <- unique(paste(refused$pathway, refused$strength,
                            refused$c_bm))
    claim(setequal(rep_cfg$key, ref_cfg),
          paste('The published rerun refused exactly the',
                'configurations that the historical check repaired.'))
  }
  if (has_rvA) {
    ref <- rvA |>
      filter(method == 'E7cr2', t1half == 0.5, c_bm == 0.45) |>
      select(N, ref = reject)
    s3a <- st_p |>
      filter(strength == 0.3, c_bm == 0.45, method == 'E7cr2',
             pathway != 'progtvgrow') |>
      left_join(ref, by = 'N')
    setv('a_n', fn(rvA_m$reps_alt))
    setv('ref35', f3(ref$ref[ref$N == 35]))
    setv('ref70', f3(ref$ref[ref$N == 70]))
    dlt <- s3a$reject - s3a$ref
    imx <- which.max(abs(dlt))
    setv('st_g9_dmax', fs3(dlt[imx]))
    claim(s3a$pathway[imx] == 'progpb' && dlt[imx] > 0,
          paste('Stress job: the largest G9 power difference from the',
                'reference is a gain under the placebo-response path.'))
  }
}
if (has_s21) {
  a <- s21 |> filter(cell == 'hybrid_null') |> arrange(method)
  b <- s21 |> filter(cell == 'progtvgrow_null') |> arrange(method)
  dd <- max(abs(a$reject - b$reject), na.rm = TRUE)
  setv('abs_dd', f4(dd))
  claim(dd == 0, 'Constant shift reproduces the null cell exactly.')
}
```

```{r values-blockN, include = FALSE}
if (has_rvN) {
  nN <- rvN |> filter(c_pb > 0)
  ids <- unique(nN$cell_id)
  pN <- rvNp |> filter(cell_id %in% ids)
  d9 <- pN |> filter(method == 'E7cr2')
  d10 <- pN |> filter(method == 'E7null_cr2')
  dF <- pN |> filter(method == 'F1')
  n_bn <- rvN_m$reps_null
  setv('bn_cpb', sprintf('%.1f', unique(nN$c_pb)))
  setv('bn_n', fn(n_bn))
  setv('bn_band', band_txt(n_bn))
  setv('bn_cells', length(ids))
  setv('bn_g9_d', rng(d9$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_g10_d', rng(d10$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_f1_d', rng(dF$diff_vs_g8, fs4))
  setv('bn_g9_z', sprintf('%.1f', min(d9$diff_vs_g8 / d9$paired_se)))
  claim(all(d9$diff_vs_g8 > 0),
        'Block N, c_pb > 0: G9 above G8 in every cell.')
  claim(all(abs(d10$diff_vs_g8) < 2 * d10$paired_se),
        'Block N, c_pb > 0: G10 within 2 paired SE of G8.')
  above <- function(m) {
    sum(nN$reject[nN$method == m & is.na(nN$h_fixed)] >
          band(n_bn)[2])
  }
  setv('bn_up_g8', above('E2cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_g9', above('E7cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_g10', above('E7null_cr2'))
  setv('bn_up_f1', above('F1'))
  claim(above('E7null_cr2') <= above('E2cr2'),
        'Block N: G10 exceeds the band in no more cells than G8.')
}
```

```{r values-gapC, include = FALSE}
if (has_gfC) {
  n_c <- gfC_m$n_reps
  n_l <- gfC_m$n_reps_large
  setv('c_n', fn(n_c))
  setv('c_band', band_txt(n_c))
  setv('l_n', fn(n_l))
  setv('l_band', band_txt(n_l))
  C1 <- gfC |>
    filter(sub == 'C1-ladder') |>
    mutate(path = case_when(c_pb > 0 ~ 'progpb',
                            c_tv > 0 ~ 'progtvconst',
                            c_bl > 0 ~ 'progbl'),
           strength = pmax(c_pb, c_tv, c_bl))
  c0 <- C1 |> filter(c_bm == 0)
  setv('c_nnull', length(unique(c0$cell_id)))
  setv('c_g9_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_g10_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('c_f1_null', rng(c0$reject[c0$method == 'F1']))
  claim(all(in_band(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7cr2'], n_c)),
        'Feasible grid: G9 null inside the band in every cell.')
  pb0 <- c0 |> filter(path == 'progpb')
  op0 <- c0 |> filter(path != 'progpb')
  setv('c_pb_g9_est', rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_pb_g10_est',
       rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7null_cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_pb_f1_est', rng(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  setv('c_op_g9_est', rng(op0$mean_est[op0$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  claim(max(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2']) <
          min(op0$mean_est[op0$method == 'E7cr2']),
        'G9 null estimate is more negative under c_pb than elsewhere.')
  claim(all(abs(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'F1']) <
              abs(pb0$mean_est[pb0$method == 'E7cr2'])),
        'F1 null estimate is nearer zero than G9 under c_pb.')
  a3 <- C1 |> filter(c_bm > 0, c_bm < 0.45)
  setv('c_bm_alt', sprintf('%.2f', unique(a3$c_bm)))
  pb3 <- a3 |> filter(path == 'progpb')
  op3 <- a3 |> filter(path != 'progpb')
  setv('c_pb_g9_pw', rng(pb3$reject[pb3$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_pb_f1_pw', rng(pb3$reject[pb3$method == 'F1']))
  setv('c_op_g9_pw', rng(op3$reject[op3$method == 'E7cr2']))
  setv('c_pb_g9_ae', rng(pb3$mean_est[pb3$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_op_g9_ae', rng(op3$mean_est[op3$method == 'E7cr2'], fs2))
  setv('c_f1_ae', rng(a3$mean_est[a3$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  if (has_ceil) {
    mx <- function(p) max(a3$strength[a3$path == p])
    setv('c_mx_pb', sprintf('%.2f', mx('progpb')))
    setv('c_mx_bl', sprintf('%.2f', mx('progbl')))
    setv('c_gap_pb', f3(bnd('c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.3') - mx('progpb')))
    setv('c_gap_bl', f3(bnd('c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3') - mx('progbl')))
  }
  C2 <- gfC |> filter(sub == 'C2-largeN')
  lg <- function(m, n_, cpb) {
    row1(C2, method == m, N == n_, c_pb == cpb)
  }
  setv('l_g9_45', f3(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g10_45', f3(lg('E7null_cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g8_45', f3(lg('E2cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g1_45', f3(lg('E1', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_f1_45', f3(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_f1a0_45', f3(lg('F1A0', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_fb_45', f3(lg('F1A0B', 280, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_30', f3(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.3)$reject))
  setv('l_f1_30', f3(lg('F1', 280, 0.3)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_140', f3(lg('E7cr2', 140, 0.45)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_70', f3(row1(C1, method == 'E7cr2', path == 'progpb',
                          strength == 0.45, c_bm == 0)$reject))
  setv('l_g9_est', fs2(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$mean_est))
  setv('l_f1_est', fs2(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$mean_est))
  setv('l_g9_k', f2(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$kappa))
  setv('l_f1_k', f2(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$kappa))
  claim(lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$reject > band(n_l)[2],
        'Large N: G9 above the band at N = 280, c_pb = 0.45.')
  claim(in_band(lg('F1', 280, 0.45)$reject, n_l) &&
          in_band(lg('F1A0B', 280, 0.45)$reject, n_l),
        'Large N: F1 and F1A0B inside the band at N = 280.')
  ff <- C2 |> filter(method %in% c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'))
  ff0 <- c0 |> filter(path == 'progpb',
                      method %in% c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'))
  claim(all(in_band(ff$reject, n_l)) && all(in_band(ff0$reject, n_c)),
        paste('The F-family stays inside the band under the',
              'placebo-response pathway at every N.'))
  claim(all(in_band(c0$reject[c0$method == 'E7null_cr2'], n_c)),
        'Feasible grid: G10 null inside the band in every cell.')
  if (has_gfCa) {
    cid <- lg('E7cr2', 280, 0.45)$cell_id
    pd <- paired_diff(gfC_all, cid, 'E7cr2', 'F1')
    setv('l_pd', fs3(pd[['diff']]))
    setv('l_pd_se', f3(pd[['se']]))
    pd2 <- paired_diff(gfC_all, cid, 'E7null_cr2', 'F1A0')
    setv('l_pd2', fs3(pd2[['diff']]))
    setv('l_pd2_se', f3(pd2[['se']]))
    claim(pd[['diff']] < -2 * pd[['se']],
          'Large N: F1 rejects less than G9 by over 2 paired SE.')
  }
}
```

```{r values-trend, include = FALSE}
if (has_rvT) {
  n_t <- rvT_m$reps_other
  tn <- function(m) row1(rvT, method == m, c_bm == 0)
  ta <- function(m) row1(rvT, method == m, c_bm == 0.45)
  setv('t_coef', sprintf('%.1f', unique(rvT$b_tv_trend)))
  setv('t_n', fn(n_t))
  setv('t_band', band_txt(n_t))
  setv('t_g8', f3(tn('E2cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_g9', f3(tn('E7cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_f1', f3(tn('F1')$reject))
  setv('t_g8_est', fs2(tn('E2cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_g9_est', fs2(tn('E7cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_f1_est', fs2(tn('F1')$mean_est))
  setv('t_g8_se', f2(tn('E2cr2')$emp_se))
  pf <- row1(rvTp, method == 'F1', grepl('cbm0.00', cell_id))
  p9 <- row1(rvTp, method == 'E7cr2', grepl('cbm0.00', cell_id))
  setv('t_f1_d', fs3(pf$diff_vs_g8))
  setv('t_f1_dse', f3(pf$paired_se))
  setv('t_g9_d', fs3(p9$diff_vs_g8))
  setv('t_g9_dse', f3(p9$paired_se))
  setv('t_g9_pw', f3(ta('E7cr2')$reject))
  setv('t_g9_aest', fs2(ta('E7cr2')$mean_est))
  setv('t_f1_pw', f3(ta('F1')$reject))
  claim(tn('E7cr2')$reject > band(n_t)[2],
        'Trend: G9 null above the band.')
  claim(in_band(tn('F1')$reject, n_t),
        'Trend: F1 null inside the band.')
  claim(tn('F1')$mean_est < tn('E2cr2')$mean_est &&
          tn('F1')$mean_est > 0,
        'Trend: F1 null estimate positive but below that of G8.')
  if (has_rvA) {
    r0 <- row1(rvA, method == 'E7cr2', t1half == 0.5, N == 70,
               c_bm == 0.45)
    setv('t_ref_pw', f3(r0$reject))
    setv('t_ref_est', fs2(r0$mean_est))
    claim(ta('E7cr2')$reject < r0$reject,
          'Trend: G9 power below the no-trend reference.')
  }
}
```

```{r values-gvf, include = FALSE}
if (has_s27) {
  t1 <- s27 |> filter(design != 'CO')
  setv('g_n', fn(s27_m$n_reps))
  setv('g_band', band_txt(s27_m$n_reps))
  nul <- t1 |> filter(c_bm == 0)
  setv('g_null_g10', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('g_null_f1a0', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1A0']))
  setv('g_null_fb', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1A0B']))
  setv('g_null_f1', rng(nul$reject[nul$method == 'F1']))
  co_f <- s27 |> filter(design == 'CO', grepl('^F', method))
  claim(all(is.na(co_f$reject)),
        'The F-family is not estimable under CO.')
  alt <- t1 |> filter(c_bm > 0)
  ratio <- function(d, m) {
    w <- alt |> filter(design == d, method %in% c(m, 'E7null_cr2')) |>
      select(cell_id, method, reject) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = reject)
    100 * mean(w[[m]]) / mean(w$E7null_cr2)
  }
  for (d in c('Hybrid', 'OLBDC')) {
    for (m in c('F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B')) {
      setv(paste0('g_r_', d, '_', m), sprintf('%.1f', ratio(d, m)))
    }
  }
  if (has_s27a) {
    pool <- function(d, m) {
      ids <- unique(alt$cell_id[alt$design == d])
      x <- vapply(ids, function(i) {
        paired_diff(s27_all, i, 'E7null_cr2', m)[c('diff', 'se')]
      }, numeric(2))
      c(diff = mean(x['diff', ]),
        se = sqrt(sum(x['se', ]^2)) / ncol(x), k = ncol(x))
    }
    for (d in c('Hybrid', 'OLBDC')) {
      for (m in c('F1', 'F1A0')) {
        p <- pool(d, m)
        setv(paste0('g_pd_', d, '_', m), fs3(p[['diff']]))
        setv(paste0('g_pse_', d, '_', m), f3(p[['se']]))
        setv('g_k', p[['k']])
      }
    }
  }
}
if (has_rvA) {
  a2 <- rvA |> filter(t1half == 2, c_bm == 0.45)
  setv('a_f1_pw', rng(a2$reject[a2$method == 'F1']))
  setv('a_g10_pw', rng(a2$reject[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2']))
  setv('a_f1_est', rng(a2$mean_est[a2$method == 'F1'], fs2))
  setv('a_g10_est', rng(a2$mean_est[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2'], fs2))
  claim(all(a2$reject[a2$method == 'F1'] <
              a2$reject[a2$method == 'E7null_cr2']),
        'Block A, t1/2 = 2: F1 below G10 in power in every cell.')
}
```

```{r values-hist, include = FALSE}
if (has_st_h && has_re_h) {
  ref_h <- re_h |>
    filter(pathway == 'none', c_bm == 0.45, method == 'G9') |>
    select(N, ref = reject)
  hh <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, method == 'E7cr2',
           pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst')) |>
    left_join(ref_h, by = 'N') |>
    mutate(loss = ref - reject)
  setv('h_ref35', f3(ref_h$ref[ref_h$N == 35]))
  setv('h_ref70', f3(ref_h$ref[ref_h$N == 70]))
  setv('h_loss6', rng(100 * hh$loss[hh$strength == 0.6],
                      function(x) sprintf('%.0f', x)))
  setv('h_loss3', f3(max(abs(hh$loss[hh$strength == 0.3]))))
  nmeth <- length(unique(st_h$method))
  setv('h_nmeth', nmeth)
  lw <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst')) |>
    select(pathway, N, method, strength, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = strength, values_from = reject,
                names_prefix = 's')
  claim(all(lw$s0.6 < lw$s0.3),
        paste('Historical: every analysis lost power at strength 0.6',
              'on the placebo-response and natural-history pathways.'))
}
if (has_pdc) {
  ps <- pdc$summary
  pv <- function(p, s, cb, w) ps[[w]][ps$pathway == p &
                                        ps$strength == s &

  setv('h_c_none', fs2(pv('none', 0, 0.45, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_c_pb6', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.6, 0.45, 'contrast_repaired')))
  setv('h_c_tv6',
       fs2(pv('progtvconst', 0.6, 0.45, 'contrast_repaired')))
  setv('h_c_pb3n', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.3, 0, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_c_pb6n', fs2(pv('progpb', 0.6, 0, 'contrast_raw')))
  setv('h_eig_pb3', f3(pv('progpb', 0.3, 0.45, 'min_eigenvalue')))
  setv('h_npaths', max(ps$paths_repaired))
  six_pd <- ps |>
    filter((pathway %in% c('progpb', 'progtvconst') &
              strength == 0.6) |

  claim(all(six_pd$paths_repaired == max(ps$paths_repaired)),
        'Historical: every infeasible cell is repaired on all paths.')
}
if (has_re_h) {

    select(cell_id, method, reject) |>

  dmx <- max(abs(c(w$G9rs, w$G9re, w$G9rse) - rep(w$G9, 3)))
  setv('re_dmax', f3(dmx))
  setv('re_ncell', nrow(w))
  setv('re_n6', length(unique(re_h$cell_id[re_h$strength == 0.6])))
  setv('re_nonconv', sprintf('%.1f', 100 * max(re_h$nonconv)))
  setv('re_reps', fn(re_h_m$n_reps))
}
if (has_m12) setv('m12_dmax', f3(max(abs(m12$diff))))
```

# Abstract {-}

**Background.** The biomarker-treatment interaction test of an
aggregated N-of-1 trial is built for a predictive biomarker. A
biomarker can also be prognostic. It can then be associated with the
natural history, the placebo response or the baseline level. We asked
when such an association biases the interaction test, and what
removes the bias.

**Methods.** We simulated the Hybrid design under the extended
data-generating process (DGP) of the companion DGP paper (paper 01), with the
parameter values published by Hendrickson et al. Five prognostic
pathways were examined. Three are correlations of the biomarker with a
component. Two are mean shifts of the natural-history component, one
constant and one growing over the trial. We compared analyses with
and without the design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$.
A second stress test, run with the driver of paper 01,
fitted ten analyses to trials with four prognostic pathways at
strength 0.3. Its analyses keep the baseline visit as an outcome row.

**Results.** Under a correlation with the placebo-response component
of 0.45, the analyses without expectancy terms rejected a true null at
`r V('l_g9_45')` (G9) at $N = 280$. With the terms, the rate was
`r V('l_f1_45')` (F1). The two-MCSE band at `r V('l_n')` replicates
was `r V('l_band')`.
Under a natural-history shift that grows over the trial, G9 rejected
at `r V('t_g9')` and F1 at `r V('t_f1')` at $N = 70$, with no
baseline row in the analysis. Without a prognostic effect, F1A0
reached `r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0')` percent of the power of G10 in the
Hybrid cells. In the second stress test, the analyses with expectancy
terms stayed inside the two-MCSE band under every pathway. Every
analysis without them, G10 included, exceeded the band under at least
one pathway. The bias from the growing shift changed sign when a
baseline row was added. The power loss once attributed to a strong
prognostic correlation came from repaired covariance matrices. Under
the current stop on infeasible matrices, all `r V('n6_refused')` of
those cells were refused.

**Conclusions.** For a biomarker that may be prognostic, add
$\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$ to the recommended analysis of the
companion carryover paper (paper 02). A biomarker that may predict the rate of
natural-history change needs a biomarker-by-time term. That remedy
has not yet been simulated.

# Notation and glossary {-}

Symbols follow `analysis/report/NOTATION.md`. Two symbols are not yet
listed there and are marked *proposed*.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $B_i$, $B^c_i$ | biomarker of participant $i$; centered at the trial's baseline mean |
| $z_i$ | standardized biomarker |
| $w_t$ | calendar week of visit $t$ |
| $c_{bm}$ | on-drug biomarker-response correlation, the interaction under the correlation encoding |
| $c_{bm,PB}$, $c_{bm,TV}$, $c_{bm,BL}$ | prognostic correlations of the biomarker with the placebo-response component, the natural-history component and the baseline level |
| $b_{TV}$ (*proposed*) | constant natural-history mean shift per SD of the biomarker |
| $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ (*proposed*) | coefficient of the trend pathway: a shift of $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i\,g(w_t)$, with $g$ the natural-history mean course scaled to peak 1 |
| $\sigma_{BR}$, $\sigma_{PB}$, $\sigma_{TV}$ | SDs of the drug-response, placebo-response and natural-history components |
| $t_{1/2}$, $t^a_{1/2}$ | carryover half-life of the DGP; half-life assumed by the analysis |
| $D_{bc,it}$ | exposure-weighted drug indicator built at $t^a_{1/2}$ |
| $\eta_t$ | design expectancy: 1 open label, 0.5 blinded, 0 at baseline |
| $\beta_{bm:D}$ | interaction coefficient, the target of the test |
| $\beta_\eta$, $\beta_{bm:\eta}$ | coefficients of $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$ |
| $\kappa$ | mean model standard error divided by the empirical SD of the estimates |
| $\hat\pi$, MCSE | estimated rejection rate and its Monte Carlo standard error |

- **Correlation encoding.** The interaction is a correlation between
  the biomarker and the drug response. It is present on drug and
  decays after discontinuation at the carryover half-life. Code
  labels it `mvn`.
- **Original DGP; extended DGP.** The original DGP is the code
  published by Hendrickson et al. at commit `58b32a9`
  [@hendrickson2020]. The extended DGP is the one recommended in
  paper 01 [@pmsimstats-paper01], which calls it the recommended DGP.
  It has a decaying biomarker-response
  correlation, the same first-order autoregressive correlation for
  every component with a constant between-component correlation at
  every lag ($\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$), carryover that decays from
  the last on-drug mean, and a stop on correlation matrices that are
  not positive definite. Code and data label it `refined`.
- **Published parameter set; simcore2026 set.** The published set is
  the component means and SDs of Hendrickson et al. Paper 01 calls
  them the default values. The simcore2026
  set is an earlier set used by the paper 02 drivers before
  2026-11-03. Runs under it are labeled historical in this draft.
- **Predictive biomarker.** One that changes the drug response
  ($c_{bm} \ne 0$). **Prognostic biomarker:** one associated with the
  outcome through another channel. A biomarker can be both.
- **Prognostic pathway.** One channel of prognostic association. The
  stored data labels are `prog-BL` ($c_{bm,BL}$), `prog-TV-const`
  ($c_{bm,TV}$), `prog-PB` ($c_{bm,PB}$), `prog-TV-grow` ($b_{TV}$,
  constant despite its label) and the block T trend pathway
  ($b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}$). The second stress test's growing
  natural-history pathway is the trend pathway under another name.
- **Baseline row.** An outcome row at week 0 holding the baseline
  level, with $D_{bc,it} = 0$ and $\eta_t = 0$. The analyses of the
  second stress test include it. Those of the paper 02 driver do not:
  their first row is the week-4 visit.
- **Feasibility bound.** The largest value of one correlation, given
  the others, for which the joint correlation matrix is positive
  definite on every path of the design.
- **Silent repair; repaired cell.** Before 2026-10-26 the drivers
  replaced a matrix that was not positive definite with a nearby one
  that was, without warning. A repaired cell is a cell simulated
  under such a matrix.
- **G-family.** Analyses with no expectancy terms. **G8:**
  $D_{bc,it}$ at the true half-life with CR2, an oracle benchmark and
  not a candidate analysis. **G9:** $t^a_{1/2}$ chosen by AIC on the
  model with the interaction, with CR2. **G10:** $t^a_{1/2}$ chosen by
  AIC on the model without the interaction, the interaction model
  refitted, with CR2. G10 is the recommended analysis of paper 02
  [@pmsimstats-paper02]. G1 and G6 are the binary-indicator analyses,
  with the working-covariance standard error and with CR2. Stored codes: `E2cr2`, `E7cr2`,
  `E7null_cr2`, `E1`, `E1cr2`.
- **F-family.** The G-family model plus $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$, with
  CR2. **F1:** $t^a_{1/2}$ fixed at the half-life policy value of 0.2
  week. **F1A:** chosen by AIC with the interaction in the model.
  **F1A0:** chosen by AIC without it. **F1A0B:** F1A0 with a
  single-resample parametric-bootstrap calibration that repeats the
  selection.
- **CR2.** The Bell-McCaffrey bias-reduced cluster-robust standard
  error with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
  [@bell2002bias; @pustejovsky2018].
- **Two-MCSE band.** The interval $0.05 \pm 2\sqrt{0.05 \times
  0.95/n}$ at $n$ replicates.
- **Designs.** Hybrid: open-label titration, then blinded
  discontinuation, then a brief crossover. OL+BDC: open-label
  titration then blinded discontinuation. CO: a two-period crossover.
- **Single-resample bootstrap.** One bootstrap resample per Monte
  Carlo replicate, with the critical value taken from the pooled
  resamples of the cell.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

An aggregated N-of-1 trial gives each participant repeated periods on
and off drug. Pooling the participants allows a test of whether a
baseline biomarker modifies the drug effect. That test targets a
predictive biomarker. The interaction test in a parallel-group trial
already needs a large sample [@brookes2004]. The N-of-1 design
reduces that cost by comparing each participant with themselves
[@senn2002; @araujo2016].

A biomarker can also be prognostic. It may track the severity at
baseline, the natural course of the illness, or the response to
placebo. In a design whose expectancy varies between open-label and
blinded phases, the on-drug and off-drug visits differ in more than
drug exposure. A prognostic association that differs between those
visits can then project onto the interaction term. The test would
then report moderation of the drug effect where there is none. A
prognostic effect is known to bias tests of a
biomarker-by-treatment interaction when the analysis model omits or
misrepresents it [@haller2018; @kent2020path].

The companion paper on carryover [@pmsimstats-paper02] studies a
predictive-only biomarker. It recommends G10. That analysis uses an
exposure-weighted drug indicator, chooses its half-life by AIC on the
model without the interaction, and tests with CR2. This paper asks
what changes when the biomarker is also prognostic. It examines five
pathways. It compares the G-family with the F-family, which adds the
design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$. It also reports
a finding about the simulation itself. An apparent loss of power
under a strong prognostic correlation came from the silent repair of
infeasible covariance matrices. It was not a property of any
analysis.

Paper 01 defines the extended DGP [@pmsimstats-paper01]. It assumes
that the biomarker is not prognostic and refers that case to this
paper. Two pieces of work that began there therefore appear here. The
first is the joint feasibility condition.
A prognostic correlation shares one feasibility condition with
$c_{bm}$, and the extended DGP refuses a matrix that violates it
(Section \@ref(sec-feasibility), Appendix \@ref(sec-jointfeas)). The
second is the prognostic cells of a stress test whose other cells
paper 01 reports. That test fitted ten analyses, each with a baseline
row, under four prognostic pathways (Section \@ref(sec-tenan)). The studies are
exploratory.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

## Data-generating process {#sec-dgp}

All published-set cells use the extended DGP under the correlation
encoding, on the Hybrid design, with $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week unless
stated. The component means and SDs are those of Hendrickson et al.
Table \@ref(tab:tab-params) reads them from the stored run metadata.
The drug-response SD is $\sigma_{BR} =$ `r V('sig_br')`. The true
interaction at $c_{bm}$ is therefore $-c_{bm}\sigma_{BR}$ per SD of
the biomarker: `r V('truth45')` at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ and
`r V('truth30')` at $c_{bm} = 0.30$. The components are reductions in
symptom severity, so an increase in any component lowers the
outcome. Interaction coefficients are negative.

```{r tab-params}
pm <- if (!is.null(gfC_m)) gfC_m else st_p_m
if (!is.null(pm$params$resp_param)) {
  rp <- pm$params$resp_param
  bp <- pm$params$baseline_param
  cat_lab <- c(tv = 'Natural history (TV)', pb = 'Placebo response (PB)',
               br = 'Drug response (BR)', bm = 'Biomarker',
               BL = 'Baseline level')
  tp <- rbind(
    data.frame(Component = cat_lab[rp$cat],
               Mean = sprintf('%.2f', rp$max),
               SD = sprintf('%g', rp$sd),
               Rate = sprintf('%.2f', rp$rate),
               Displacement = sprintf('%g', rp$disp)),
    data.frame(Component = cat_lab[bp$cat],
               Mean = sprintf('%.1f', bp$m),
               SD = sprintf('%.1f', bp$sd),
               Rate = '--', Displacement = '--'))
  rownames(tp) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(tp, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c('Component', 'Maximum or mean', 'SD',
                  'Rate (per week)', 'Displacement'),
    caption = 'Parameter values of the published-set runs, read from
      the stored run metadata (\\texttt{meta.rds}, field
      \\texttt{params}). For the
      response components the mean column is the maximum $m$ of the
      modified Gompertz curve.') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the parameter table of the published-set runs')
}
```

## Prognostic pathways {#sec-pathways}

A biomarker may be associated with the outcome through channels other
than the drug response. Three pathways are entries in the biomarker
row of the joint correlation matrix. Each sets one correlation with
the others at zero. The first is a correlation with the baseline
level, $c_{bm,BL}$. The second is a correlation with the
natural-history component at every visit, $c_{bm,TV}$. The third is a
correlation with the placebo-response component at every visit,
$c_{bm,PB}$. Their strengths are bounded by feasibility (Section
\@ref(sec-feasibility)).

Two further pathways are mean shifts. They are not bounded by the
correlation matrix. The constant shift adds $b_{TV}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i$
to the natural-history mean at every visit. It is stored as
`prog-TV-grow` although it does not grow. It is absorbed exactly by
the biomarker main effect of every analysis here (Appendix
\@ref(sec-absorb)). It serves only as a check of that absorption. The
trend pathway adds $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}}\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i\,g(w_t)$,
where $g$ is the natural-history mean course scaled to peak 1. It
describes a biomarker that predicts the rate of natural-history
change. A model with no biomarker-by-time term cannot absorb it.

## Analyses {#sec-analyses}

All analyses fit a linear mixed model with a participant random
intercept and continuous-time AR(1) residual correlation
(`corCAR1`). The G-family model is
$$
Y_{it} = \beta_0 + \beta_B B^c_i + \beta_T w_t + \beta_D D_{bc,it}
  + \beta_{bm:D} B^c_i D_{bc,it} + u_i + \epsilon_{it}.
$$
$D_{bc,it}$ is one on drug, $2^{-t_{sd}/t^a_{1/2}}$ off drug after
first exposure, and zero before first exposure. G8 sets
$t^a_{1/2} = t_{1/2}$. It is an oracle benchmark and not a candidate
analysis. G9 chooses $t^a_{1/2}$ by maximum-likelihood AIC over
$\{0.25, 0.5, 1, 2\}$ weeks with the interaction in the model
[@akaike1974new]. G10 makes the same choice on the model without the
interaction and refits the interaction model by REML. The selection
of G9 depends on the coefficient under test. That is a
post-selection inference risk [@berk2013valid; @leeb2005]. All three
test $\beta_{bm:D}$ with CR2 and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

The F-family adds the design-expectancy terms:
$$
Y_{it} = \ldots + \beta_\eta \eta_t + \beta_{bm:\eta} B^c_i \eta_t.
$$
The regressors are `De` and `bmc:De`. The placebo-response amplitude
scales with $\eta_t$, and $\eta_t$ differs between on-drug and
off-drug visits in the Hybrid design. A biomarker correlated with the
placebo response therefore acquires an on/off slope difference by
construction. The term $B^c_i\eta_t$ absorbs it. F1 fixes
$t^a_{1/2}$ at 0.2 week. F1A selects it by AIC with the interaction.
F1A0 selects it without the interaction, as G10 does. F1A0B
calibrates F1A0 by a single-resample parametric bootstrap under the
null that repeats the selection. Its candidate grid is $\{0, 0.2,
0.5, 1, 2\}$ weeks. $\eta_t$ is constant within every path of the
crossover design. The F-family is therefore not estimable under CO.
F1A0 and G10 differ only in the expectancy terms. That is the
property that lets this paper and paper 02 give one recommendation
(Section \@ref(sec-recommend)).

## Performance measures {#sec-perf}

We report the rejection rate $\hat\pi$ at $\alpha = 0.05$, its MCSE,
the mean interaction estimate, and $\kappa$ [@morris2019simulation].
Under the null $\hat\pi$ is the Type I error. A cell's rejection rate
is compared with its two-MCSE band. That band is a check on gross
departures and not a demonstration of nominal size. Within a job,
cells at the same design and $N$ share random-number streams, and
every analysis is fitted to the same trials. Contrasts between
analyses are paired, and their standard errors come from the
per-replicate rejection indicators. Comparisons across jobs are
unpaired. Results from different simulation hosts are not
draw-for-draw identical.

## Stored runs and their parameter sets {#sec-sources}

Table \@ref(tab:tab-sources) lists every stored run this draft reads.
The second stress test of Section \@ref(sec-tenan) comes from another
driver, the stress test of paper 01.
The published-set runs are the reruns of `docs/74`. The historical
runs used the simcore2026 parameter set and silent repair. They are
kept only as the exhibit of Section \@ref(sec-artifact)
(`docs/74`, decision D5). No historical number enters a result about
an analysis.

```{r tab-sources}
srow <- function(what, folder, meta, kind, set = NULL, base = 'cs',
                 date = NULL) {
  folder <- if (base == 'cs') {
    paste0('carryover-sensitivity/', folder)
  } else {
    paste0('quick-sim/carryover-closed-form/', folder)
  }
  data.frame(
    Run = what,
    Folder = paste0('\\texttt{', gsub('_', '\\\\_', folder), '}'),
    Set = if (!is.null(set)) set else

    Date = if (!is.null(date)) date else
      if (is.null(meta) || is.null(meta$date)) '--' else format(as.Date(meta$date)),
    Kind = kind)
}

knitr::kable(tsrc, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
```

# Results {#sec-results}

## Feasibility of a prognostic correlation {#sec-feasibility}

A prognostic correlation occupies the same biomarker row of the
correlation matrix as $c_{bm}$. The two therefore share one
feasibility condition. Writing the row as a sum of fixed patterns
scaled by the correlations, the condition becomes a quadratic form in
the correlations that must be below one. The largest value of one
correlation given the others is the positive root of a quadratic
(Appendix \@ref(sec-jointfeas)). Table \@ref(tab:tab-jointceil) gives
the bounds for the Hybrid design under the extended DGP. They depend
on the correlation matrix only, not on the component SDs, so they
hold for both parameter sets.

```{r values-jointceil, include = FALSE}
jc_file <- file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                     'carryover-closed-form', 'rho-stage',
                     'prognostic-joint-ceilings.csv')
has_jc <- file.exists(jc_file)
if (has_jc) {
  jc <- read.csv(jc_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  jc_v <- function(d, th, cp, g) {
    jc$ceiling[jc$design == d & jc$t1half == th & jc$coupling == cp &
                 jc$given == g]
  }
  setv('jc_gap45', f3(jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45') - 0.3))
  setv('jc_bm02', f2(jc_v('Hybrid', 0.2, 'c_bm', 'c_pb = 0.3')))
  setv('jc_co_pb', f3(jc_v('CO', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'alone')))
  setv('jc_hy_pb', f3(jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'alone')))
  hy <- jc[jc$design == 'Hybrid', ]
  ob <- jc[jc$design == 'OLBDC', ]
  k <- match(paste(hy$t1half, hy$coupling, hy$given),
             paste(ob$t1half, ob$coupling, ob$given))
  setv('jc_ob_dmax', f3(max(abs(hy$ceiling - ob$ceiling[k]),
                            na.rm = TRUE)))
  claim(all(is.na(jc$ceiling[jc$given == 'c_pb = 0.6'])),
        'Joint bounds: no c_bm is feasible with c_bm,PB = 0.6.')
  claim(jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'c_bm = 0.45') > 0.3 &&
          jc_v('Hybrid', 0.2, 'c_bm', 'c_pb = 0.3') < 0.45,
        paste('Joint bounds: strength 0.3 is feasible with c_bm = 0.45',
              'at 0.5 week but not at 0.2 week.'))
  claim(jc_v('CO', 0.5, 'c_bm', 'alone') >
          jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_bm', 'alone') &&
          jc_v('CO', 0.5, 'c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3') >
          jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_bl', 'c_bm = 0.3') &&
          jc_v('CO', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'alone') <
          jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, 'c_pb', 'alone'),
        paste('Joint bounds: CO is looser than Hybrid on c_bm and',
              'c_bm,BL and tighter on c_bm,PB alone.'))
  claim(all(jc$min_eig_below > 0, na.rm = TRUE) &&
          all(jc$min_eig_above < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        paste('Joint bounds: the smallest eigenvalue is positive just',
              'below each bound and negative just above it.'))
  if (has_ceil) {
    cr0 <- ceil$results
    cr0 <- cr0[cr0$coupling != 'c_tv' & !grepl('c_tv', cr0$given), ]
    ck <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cr0)), function(i) {
      v <- jc_v('Hybrid', 0.5, cr0$coupling[i], cr0$given[i])
      length(v) == 1 && isTRUE(all.equal(v, cr0$ceiling[i]))
    }, logical(1))
    claim(all(ck[!is.na(cr0$ceiling)]),
          paste('The historical ceiling file and the joint-ceiling',
                'table agree at Hybrid, 0.5 week.'))
  }
}
```

```{r tab-jointceil}
if (has_jc) {
  jc_hyb <- jc[jc$design == 'Hybrid' & jc$t1half %in% c(0.2, 0.5), ]
  jc_rows <- data.frame(
    lab = c('$c_{bm,PB}$ or $c_{bm,TV}$', '', '', '',
            '$c_{bm,BL}$', '', '', '', '$c_{bm}$', '', ''),
    given = c('alone', '$c_{bm} = 0.25$', '$c_{bm} = 0.30$',
              '$c_{bm} = 0.45$', 'alone', '$c_{bm} = 0.25$',
              '$c_{bm} = 0.30$', '$c_{bm} = 0.45$', 'alone',
              '$c_{bm,PB} = 0.3$', '$c_{bm,PB} = 0.6$'),
    key_c = c(rep('c_pb', 4), rep('c_bl', 4), rep('c_bm', 3)),
    key_g = c('alone', 'c_bm = 0.25', 'c_bm = 0.3', 'c_bm = 0.45',
              'alone', 'c_bm = 0.25', 'c_bm = 0.3', 'c_bm = 0.45',
              'alone', 'c_pb = 0.3', 'c_pb = 0.6'))
  jc_pick <- function(th) {
    vapply(seq_len(nrow(jc_rows)), function(i) {
      v <- jc_hyb$ceiling[jc_hyb$t1half == th &
                            jc_hyb$coupling == jc_rows$key_c[i] &
                            jc_hyb$given == jc_rows$key_g[i]]
      if (length(v) != 1 || is.na(v)) 'none' else sprintf('%.3f', v)
    }, character(1))
  }
  jc_tab <- data.frame(jc_rows$lab, jc_rows$given, jc_pick(0.2),
                       jc_pick(0.5))
  knitr::kable(jc_tab, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Correlation', 'Given', '$t_{1/2} = 0.2$ week',
                  '$t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week'),
    caption = 'Largest feasible prognostic correlation given the
      biomarker-response correlation $c_{bm}$, and the reverse, under
      the extended DGP (separable AR(1), $\\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$),
      Hybrid design, minimum over its four paths. Correlation: the
      quantity whose bound is given. $c_{bm,PB}$, $c_{bm,TV}$,
      $c_{bm,BL}$: correlation of the biomarker with the
      placebo-response component, the natural-history component and
      the baseline level. None: no value is feasible. Computed from
      the correlation matrix, no simulation
      (\\texttt{18-prognostic-joint-ceiling.R}).') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the joint feasibility bounds')
}
```

At this paper's half-life of 0.5 week, a prognostic correlation of
0.3 lies inside the feasible region at every $c_{bm}$ up to 0.45, by
`r V('jc_gap45')` at 0.45. At 0.2 week it is feasible only up to
$c_{bm} =$ `r V('jc_bm02')`. A prognostic correlation of 0.6 with the
placebo-response or natural-history component is infeasible with any
$c_{bm}$. That is the combination that the repaired runs of Section
\@ref(sec-artifact) simulated. The correlations with the
placebo-response and the natural-history components have identical
bounds, because their patterns are the same constant on every visit
of one component. A correlation with the baseline level has a looser
bound. The baseline level is uncorrelated with the response
components and enters only through its square. Outside the table,
the OL+BDC bounds are within `r V('jc_ob_dmax')` of the Hybrid
values at the same half-life. The crossover bounds are looser on
$c_{bm}$ and $c_{bm,BL}$, and slightly tighter on $c_{bm,PB}$ alone
(`r V('jc_co_pb')` against `r V('jc_hy_pb')`). Each bound was checked
by the sign of the smallest eigenvalue of the full matrix: positive
at 0.999 times the bound and negative at 1.001 times it. The feasible
grid of Section \@ref(sec-grid) was chosen from these bounds.

## Correlation pathways at strength 0.3 {#sec-stress}

We crossed the three correlation pathways and the constant shift
with $c_{bm} \in \{0, 0.45\}$ and $N \in \{35, 70\}$, at
`r V('st_n')` replicates per cell. Table \@ref(tab:tab-stress) gives
the rejection rates. The two-MCSE band is `r V('st_band')`.

```{r tab-stress}
if (has_st_p) {
  ts <- st_p |>
    filter(strength == 0.3, method %in% show_m) |>
    mutate(Pathway = path_lab[pathway], Method = m_lab[method]) |>
    select(pathway, Pathway, c_bm, N, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    arrange(match(pathway, path_ord), c_bm, N) |>
    select(Pathway, c_bm, N, all_of(show_c)) |>
    mutate(c_bm = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
           across(all_of(show_c), f3))
  ts$Pathway[duplicated(ts$Pathway)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(ts, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Pathway', '$c_{bm}$', '$N$', show_c),
    caption = sprintf('Rejection rate under each prognostic pathway
      at strength 0.3, published parameter set. Hybrid, $t_{1/2} =
      0.5$ week, %s replicates per cell, the same trials for every
      analysis. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ are Type I error (band %s).
      G8 is the oracle benchmark.', V('st_n'), V('st_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set prognostic stress test')
}
```

The G9 Type I error was `r V('st_g9_null')` across the six null cells
of the three correlation pathways. G10 gave `r V('st_g10_null')` and
F1A0B `r V('st_fb_null')`. Every G9 and G10 null rate was inside the
band. The G9 power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ was `r V('st_g9_alt')`. The
no-confound reference from block A of the referee-variant runs is
`r V('ref35')` at $N = 35$ and `r V('ref70')` at $N = 70$. The
largest difference from it was `r V('st_g9_dmax')`, under the
placebo-response pathway. Section \@ref(sec-grid) shows that this
excess is bias in the estimate. That comparison is
unpaired, against `r V('a_n')`-replicate cells of another job. F1A0B
differed from G10 in power by `r V('st_fb_g10')` on the same trials.
The constant shift gave the same rejection at strengths 0.3 and 0.6
in every analysis. In the scenario job, the constant-shift null cell
differs from the unshifted Hybrid null cell by at most
`r V('abs_dd')` in any analysis. That is the absorption of Appendix
\@ref(sec-absorb).

A longer run at the placebo-response pathway sharpens the size
comparison. Block N of the referee-variant runs fitted G8, G9, G10
and F1 to `r V('bn_n')` replicates in each of `r V('bn_cells')`
Hybrid null cells at $c_{bm,PB} =$ `r V('bn_cpb')`
(Table \@ref(tab:tab-blockN)). The band is `r V('bn_band')`. The
paired difference from G8 was `r V('bn_g9_d')` for G9, `r V('bn_g10_d')`
for G10 and `r V('bn_f1_d')` for F1. G9 was above G8 in every cell,
by at least `r V('bn_g9_z')` paired standard errors. G10 was within
two paired standard errors of G8 in every cell. The number of cells
above the band was `r V('bn_up_g8')` for G8, `r V('bn_up_g9')` for
G9, `r V('bn_up_g10')` for G10 and `r V('bn_up_f1')` for F1.


## The feasible prognostic grid {#sec-grid}

A further study (driver 32, block C) ran a grid of correlations
chosen inside the feasibility bounds. At $c_{bm} = 0.30$ it set $c_{bm,PB}$ and
$c_{bm,TV}$ at 0.40 and 0.45, and $c_{bm,BL}$ at 0.6 and 0.8. It also
ran $c_{bm,BL} = 0.45$ at $c_{bm} = 0.45$. Each cell was run with and
without a true interaction, at $N = 70$ and `r V('c_n')` replicates.
The strongest $c_{bm,PB}$ lies `r V('c_gap_pb')` below its bound at
$c_{bm} = 0.30$. The strongest $c_{bm,BL}$ lies `r V('c_gap_bl')`
below its bound. Table \@ref(tab:tab-grid) gives the rejection rates
and Table \@ref(tab:tab-grid-est) the mean estimates.
