The G9 Type I error was `r V('c_g9_null')` across the
`r V('c_nnull')` null cells, inside the band in every one. G10 gave
`r V('c_g10_null')` and F1 `r V('c_f1_null')`. The rejection rates
hide a bias that the mean estimates show. Under the placebo-response
pathway with no true interaction, the mean G9 estimate was
`r V('c_pb_g9_est')`. G10 gave `r V('c_pb_g10_est')`. F1 gave
`r V('c_pb_f1_est')`. Under the other two pathways the mean G9
estimate was `r V('c_op_g9_est')`. At $c_{bm} =$ `r V('c_bm_alt')`
the same bias appears as excess power. G9 reached `r V('c_pb_g9_pw')`
under the placebo-response pathway and `r V('c_op_g9_pw')` under the
others. Its mean estimate was `r V('c_pb_g9_ae')` and
`r V('c_op_g9_ae')` against a true value of `r V('truth30')`. F1
reached `r V('c_pb_f1_pw')` under the placebo-response pathway. Its
mean estimate was `r V('c_f1_ae')` across the grid. The F1 estimate
is attenuated because its fixed half-life of 0.2 week is below the
true 0.5 week (Section \@ref(sec-gvf)). The excess power of the
G-family under the placebo-response pathway is therefore not evidence
of better power. It is the same bias as under the null.

## Larger samples under the placebo-response pathway {#sec-largen}

A bias of a fixed size becomes Type I error inflation as $N$ grows,
because the standard error shrinks. The same study ran the
placebo-response pathway with no true interaction at $N \in \{140,
280\}$ and $c_{bm,PB} \in \{0.30, 0.45\}$, at `r V('l_n')`
replicates. The band is `r V('l_band')`. Table \@ref(tab:tab-largen)
gives the result.

```{r tab-largen}
if (has_gfC) {
  tl <- gfC |>
    filter(sub == 'C2-largeN' |
             (sub == 'C1-ladder' & c_pb == 0.45 & c_bm == 0)) |>
    filter(method %in% c('E1', show_m)) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = sprintf('$c_{bm,PB} = %.2f$, $N = %d$', c_pb, N)) |>
    arrange(c_pb, N) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    select(Cell, G1, all_of(show_c)) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tl, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Type I error under the placebo-response
      pathway at larger samples, published parameter set. Hybrid,
      $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, $c_{bm} = 0$, %s replicates at $N = 140$
      and $280$ (band %s). The $N = 70$ row is from the feasible grid
      at %s replicates.', V('l_n'), V('l_band'), V('c_n'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set large-sample cells')
}
```

At $N = 280$ and $c_{bm,PB} = 0.45$, G9 rejected at
`r V('l_g9_45')`, G10 at `r V('l_g10_45')` and G8 at `r V('l_g8_45')`.
The binary-indicator analysis with the working-covariance standard
error, G1, rejected at
`r V('l_g1_45')`. The F-family stayed inside the band: F1 at
`r V('l_f1_45')`, F1A0 at `r V('l_f1a0_45')` and F1A0B at
`r V('l_fb_45')`. On the same trials, the paired difference in
rejection of F1 minus G9 was `r V('l_pd')` (paired SE
`r V('l_pd_se')`). That of F1A0 minus G10 was `r V('l_pd2')`
(`r V('l_pd2_se')`). The G9 rate rose with $N$:
`r V('l_g9_70')` at 70, `r V('l_g9_140')` at 140 and
`r V('l_g9_45')` at 280. Its mean estimate at $N = 280$ was
`r V('l_g9_est')` against `r V('l_f1_est')` for F1. The standard
errors were calibrated for both, with $\kappa$ of `r V('l_g9_k')` and
`r V('l_f1_k')`. The excess is therefore bias, not an
underestimated standard error. At $c_{bm,PB} = 0.30$ the rates were
`r V('l_g9_30')` for G9 and `r V('l_f1_30')` for F1.

## The trend pathway {#sec-trend}

Block T of the referee-variant runs simulated a natural-history shift
that grows over the trial, with $b_{TV}^{\mathrm{tr}} =$
`r V('t_coef')`. It is a mean shift, so the feasibility bound does
not limit it. G8, G9 and F1 were fitted at $N = 70$ and
`r V('t_n')` replicates (Table \@ref(tab:tab-trend)). The band is
`r V('t_band')`.

```{r tab-trend}
if (has_rvT) {
  tt <- rvT |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Cell = ifelse(c_bm == 0, 'null ($c_{bm} = 0$)',
                         sprintf('$c_{bm} = %.2f$', c_bm))) |>
    arrange(c_bm, match(method, show_m)) |>
    transmute(Cell, Method,
              Rejection = sprintf('%.3f (%.3f)', reject, mcse),
              `Mean estimate` = fs2(mean_est),
              `Empirical SE` = f2(emp_se),
              `$\\kappa$` = f2(kappa))
  tt$Cell[duplicated(tt$Cell)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(tt, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Block T, published parameter set: rejection
      rate (MCSE), mean interaction estimate, empirical SE and
      calibration ratio under the trend pathway
      ($b_{TV}^{\\mathrm{tr}} = %s$). Hybrid, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} =
      0.5$ week, %s replicates. The true value is 0 at the null and
      %s at $c_{bm} = 0.45$. Band at the null %s.', V('t_coef'),
      V('t_n'), V('truth45'), V('t_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('block T of the published-set referee-variant runs')
}
```

The trend pathway biased the G-family. Under the null G8 rejected at
`r V('t_g8')` and G9 at `r V('t_g9')`. Their mean estimates were
`r V('t_g8_est')` and `r V('t_g9_est')` where the truth is zero. The
G8 empirical SE was `r V('t_g8_se')`. F1 rejected at `r V('t_f1')`,
with a mean estimate of `r V('t_f1_est')`. Paired against G8, F1
differed by `r V('t_f1_d')` (SE `r V('t_f1_dse')`) and G9 by
`r V('t_g9_d')` (`r V('t_g9_dse')`). The expectancy terms therefore
absorb part of the shift but not all of it. At $c_{bm} = 0.45$ the
bias is toward zero. G9 power was `r V('t_g9_pw')` with a mean
estimate of `r V('t_g9_aest')`. In the no-trend cell of block A it
was `r V('t_ref_pw')` with `r V('t_ref_est')`. That comparison is
unpaired. The mechanism is the design. In the Hybrid design
$D_{bc,it}$ falls with calendar time, so a biomarker that predicts
the trend projects onto the interaction term of a model with no
biomarker-by-time term. The paper 02 driver has no baseline row. The
second stress test applied the same shift to analyses with a
baseline row and found a bias of the opposite sign (Section
\@ref(sec-reconcile)).

## A second stress test: ten analyses under the extended DGP {#sec-tenan}

This section reports the prognostic cells of a second stress test, run
with the driver of paper 01
(`analysis/scripts/quick-sim/carryover-closed-form/11-strawman-stress-test.R`).
Paper 01 reports the cells of the same study, its study 2, that have
no prognostic pathway [@pmsimstats-paper01]. The trials come from the
extended DGP with the published parameter set, in the Hybrid design:
$N = 70$ with fixed allocation (18, 18, 17, 17), $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week,
$\rho = 0.7$ and $c_1 = 0.2$. Four null cells ($c_{bm} = 0$) each add
one prognostic pathway of strength 0.3: $c_{bm,TV} = 0.3$,
$c_{bm,PB} = 0.3$, $c_{bm,BL} = 0.3$, and a mean shift of the
natural-history component of 0.3 of its SD per SD of the biomarker at
the end of its curve, growing along the curve. The last is labeled the
growing natural-history pathway here. It is not the stored
`prog-TV-grow` cell of the paper 02 driver, which is constant (Section
\@ref(sec-pathways)). It is the trend pathway of Section
\@ref(sec-trend), with the same coefficient (Section
\@ref(sec-reconcile)). Each cell has 1,000 replicates, so the
single-cell two-MCSE band is 0.036 to 0.064.

Fourteen analyses were fitted to the same trials, and ten are
reported. They are named by their model in Table
\@ref(tab:tab-tenan), not by the G and F codes of this paper. Every
one of them keeps the baseline visit as an outcome row. The
expectancy-term model adds $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$, as the F-family
does. The free-baseline model adds `bmc:bl0`, a separate biomarker
slope for the baseline row. Analyses with a fixed analysis half-life
use 0.5 week, the true value.

The study was run three times with the same seed rule,
$20261007 + 1000 \times \text{cell} + \text{chunk}$. The first run
used the compounding carryover rule on the mean and fixed allocation.
The second used carryover decaying from the last on-drug mean and
randomized allocation. The third, reported here, is the extended DGP
as defined: decaying carryover and fixed allocation. It differs from
the first only in the carryover rule and from the second only in the
allocation. Failed fits were excluded from the denominator. They
were at most 0.6% in any cell. The study is exploratory. Its cells and
analyses followed a working protocol that was revised as results came
in. Two cells with a prognostic association with baseline severity,
and three analyses, were added after the first results.

```{r p01-stress, include = FALSE}
## Paper 01's study 2 (driver 11; numbered study 3 in paper 01 before
## 2026-11-11), moved here on 2026-11-11 with its prognostic cells.
## Main run plus the two post hoc files fitted to the same trials; S
## is refitted in each post hoc file as a pairing check and dropped
## there.
ss_dir <- file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                    'carryover-closed-form', 'strawman-stress')
ss_read <- function(tag) {
  x <- lapply(c('summary-full', 'summary-full-extra',
                'summary-full-extra2'), function(b) {
    d <- read.csv(file.path(ss_dir, paste0(b, tag, '.csv')))
    if (b != 'summary-full') d <- d[d$analysis != 'S', ]
    d[, c('label', 'cbm', 'analysis', 'reject', 'fits')]
  })
  do.call(rbind, x)
}
## Third run (the reported one): the extended DGP with fixed
## allocation. Second run: randomized allocation. First run:
## compounding carryover rule.
ss3 <- ss_read('-anchored-fixed-ha0.5')
ss2 <- ss_read('-anchored')
ss1 <- ss_read('')
ss_r <- function(d, lab, an, cbm = 0) {
  v <- d$reject[d$label == lab & d$cbm == cbm & d$analysis == an]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v
}
ss_f <- function(v) sprintf('%.3f', v)
ss_an <- c(
  R = 'Binary-indicator analysis (random intercept, model-based)',
  S = 'Random intercept + CAR(1), CR2',
  DS = 'The same, half-life chosen by AIC',
  A = 'Unstructured covariance, Kenward-Roger',
  DA = 'The same, half-life chosen by AIC',
  F1 = 'Random intercept + CAR(1) with expectancy terms, CR2',
  G1 = 'The same, with phase-specific residual variances, CR2',
  G2 = 'The same, with phase-specific residual variances, model-based',
  F1A = 'Expectancy terms, half-life chosen by AIC, CR2',
  ES = 'Random intercept + CAR(1) with free baseline slope, CR2')
ss_short <- c(
  R = 'the binary-indicator analysis',
  S = 'the CAR(1) model with CR2',
  DS = 'the CAR(1) model with AIC-chosen half-life',
  A = 'the unstructured model',
  DA = 'the unstructured model with AIC-chosen half-life',
  F1 = 'the expectancy-term model',
  G1 = paste('the expectancy-term model with phase-specific',
             'variances (CR2)'),
  G2 = paste('the expectancy-term model with phase-specific',
             'variances (model-based)'),
  F1A = 'the expectancy-term model with AIC-chosen half-life',
  ES = 'the free-baseline model')
ss_prog <- c('prog-TV-const', 'prog-TV-grow', 'prog-PB', 'prog-BL')
ss_cell <- c(`prog-TV-const` = 'the constant natural-history pathway',
             `prog-TV-grow` = 'the growing natural-history pathway',
             `prog-PB` = 'the placebo pathway',
             `prog-BL` = 'the baseline-severity pathway')
ss_tab <- function(d) {
  sapply(ss_prog, function(l) {
    sapply(names(ss_an), function(a) ss_r(d, l, a))
  })
}
ss_m3 <- ss_tab(ss3)
ss_m2 <- ss_tab(ss2)
ss_m1 <- ss_tab(ss1)
ss_bold <- function(m) {
  matrix(ifelse(m > 0.075, sprintf('\\textbf{%.3f}', m),
                sprintf('%.3f', m)),
         nrow(m), dimnames = dimnames(m))
}
ss_band1 <- 0.05 + c(-2, 2) * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / 1000)
## Cells of the reported run whose classification differs from an
## earlier run, against the bold threshold (0.075) and the single-cell
## band. The first run isolates the carryover rule, the second the
## allocation.
ss_cross <- function(m, run, thr) {
  k <- which((m > thr) != (ss_m3 > thr), arr.ind = TRUE)
  if (!nrow(k)) return('none')
  paste(sprintf('%s under %s (%s run %s, third run %s)',
                ss_short[rownames(ss_m3)[k[, 1]]],
                ss_cell[colnames(ss_m3)[k[, 2]]], run,
                ss_f(m[k]), ss_f(ss_m3[k])), collapse = '; ')
}
ss_dmax_at <- function(m) {
  d <- abs(ss_m3 - m)
  k <- which(d == max(d), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
  sprintf('%s, for %s under %s', ss_f(max(d)),
          ss_short[rownames(ss_m3)[k[1]]],
          ss_cell[colnames(ss_m3)[k[2]]])
}
## The text below states these for all three runs.
for (ss_m in list(ss_m1, ss_m2, ss_m3)) {
  stopifnot(all(ss_m[c('F1', 'G1', 'G2', 'F1A'), ] < ss_band1[2]),
            all(apply(ss_m[c('R', 'S', 'DS', 'A', 'DA'), ], 1, max) >
                ss_band1[2]),
            max(ss_m['ES', ]) < ss_band1[2] + 0.015)
}
stopifnot(max(ss_m1['ES', ]) < ss_band1[2],
          which.max(ss_m2['ES', ]) == 2,
          max(ss_m2['ES', ]) > ss_band1[2],
          which.max(ss_m3['ES', ]) == 2,
          max(ss_m3['ES', ]) > ss_band1[2])
p01_pend <- function(ok, x) if (ok) x else '\\textbf{[pending]}'
```

```{r tab-tenan}
ss_tab3 <- data.frame(Analysis = unname(ss_an), ss_bold(ss_m3),
                      check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ss_tab3, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE, linesep = '',
  col.names = c('Analysis', 'Natural history, constant',
                'Natural history, growing', 'Placebo response',
                'Baseline severity'),
  caption = 'Second stress test: null rejection rates under a
    prognostic biomarker ($c_{bm} = 0$). Each pathway has strength
    0.3: a correlation of 0.3 with the natural-history component
    (constant), the placebo-response component or baseline severity,
    and for the growing natural-history pathway a mean shift of the
    natural-history component of 0.3 of its SD (3 points) per SD of
    biomarker at the end of its curve, growing along the curve. 1,000
    replicates per cell (two-MCSE band 0.036 to 0.064 for a single
    cell). Third run: the extended DGP, with carryover decaying from
    the last on-drug mean and fixed path allocation. Every analysis
    has a baseline row. Rates above 0.075 in bold. The first run is
    in Appendix \\ref{sec-firstrun}.') |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = '5.5cm') |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5, width = '2.1cm')
```

Analyses that keep baseline as an outcome row use one biomarker main
effect for baseline and for the off-drug visits. When the biomarker is
prognostic through a pathway that is absent at baseline, those two
associations differ, and part of the difference is attributed to the
interaction (Appendix \@ref(sec-shared)). Every analysis that shares
the biomarker effect with baseline exceeded the nominal level in at
least one such cell (Table \@ref(tab:tab-tenan)).

The expectancy-term family stayed within the single-cell two-MCSE band
in every prognostic cell. Its four analyses rejected
`r ss_f(min(ss_m3[c('F1', 'G1', 'G2', 'F1A'), ]))` to
`r ss_f(max(ss_m3[c('F1', 'G1', 'G2', 'F1A'), ]))`. This family adds
the expectancy and a biomarker-by-expectancy term to the mean model,
with or without residual variances that differ by trial phase. The
free-baseline model rejected `r ss_f(ss_m3['ES', 'prog-TV-grow'])`
under the growing natural-history pathway, above the single-cell band,
and `r ss_f(ss_m3['ES', 'prog-PB'])` under the placebo pathway.
Appendix \@ref(sec-shared) explains why freeing the baseline slope
alone is not sufficient when the prognostic slope grows over time or
scales with the expectancy. A prognostic association with baseline
severity alone did less harm, because baseline severity enters every
visit equally. The binary-indicator analysis rejected
`r ss_f(ss_m3['R', 'prog-BL'])` there. The scenarios in which the
pathway is absent at baseline are the ones that show the inflation.
Whether such a pathway, at a magnitude of 0.3, is realistic for blood
pressure in PTSD is not known.

**Changes between runs.** Treating two runs as independent, the
difference between them in one cell has a Monte Carlo SE of about
0.010 at a rate of 0.05. The first and third runs use the same seeds
and allocation, so their differences are paired and that SE overstates
their noise. The carryover rule changed the table by at most
`r ss_dmax_at(ss_m1)` (Appendix \@ref(sec-firstrun)). Cells that
crossed the bold threshold of 0.075:
`r ss_cross(ss_m1, 'first', 0.075)`. Cells that crossed the upper edge
of the single-cell band: `r ss_cross(ss_m1, 'first', ss_band1[2])`.
Randomized allocation changed it by at most `r ss_dmax_at(ss_m2)`.
Cells that crossed the bold threshold:
`r ss_cross(ss_m2, 'second', 0.075)`. Cells that crossed the upper edge
of the single-cell band: `r ss_cross(ss_m2, 'second', ss_band1[2])`.
In all three runs the expectancy-term family stayed within the
single-cell band in every prognostic cell. The binary-indicator, CAR(1)
and unstructured analyses each exceeded it in at least one cell, with
or without an AIC-chosen half-life. Taken analysis by analysis, only
the free-baseline model changed its classification. It stayed within
the band in the first run and exceeded it under the growing pathway in
the other two, by at most
`r ss_f(max(ss_m2['ES', ], ss_m3['ES', ]) - ss_band1[2])`.

```{r p01-g10, include = FALSE}
## G10 on the trials of the reported run (driver 11 --extra5, athena
## job 20; S refitted as the pairing check).
x5_file <- file.path(ss_dir,
                     'summary-full-extra5-anchored-fixed-ha0.5.csv')
have_x5 <- file.exists(x5_file)
if (have_x5) {
  x5 <- read.csv(x5_file)
  x5_r <- function(lab, an = 'G10', cbm = 0) {
    v <- x5$reject[x5$label == lab & abs(x5$cbm - cbm) < 1e-9 &
                     x5$analysis == an]
    stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
    v
  }
  ## Pairing: S refitted on the same trials reproduces the main run.
  x5_pair <- max(abs(mapply(function(l, cb) x5_r(l, 'S', cb) -
                              ss_r(ss3, l, 'S', cb),
                            x5$label[x5$analysis == 'S'],
                            x5$cbm[x5$analysis == 'S'])))
  stopifnot(x5_pair < 0.005)
  x5_prog <- sapply(ss_prog, x5_r)
  ## Cost of robustness: the factor by which N must grow for the
  ## expectancy-term model to match G10's power, by the normal
  ## approximation, over the separable power-curve cells with power
  ## between 0.1 and 0.95 for both.
  x5_cb <- c(0.15, 0.225, 0.30, 0.375, 0.45)
  x5_pg <- sapply(x5_cb, function(cb) x5_r('curve-C07', 'G10', cb))
  x5_pf <- sapply(x5_cb, function(cb) ss_r(ss3, 'curve-C07', 'F1', cb))
  x5_ok <- x5_pg > 0.1 & x5_pg < 0.95 & x5_pf > 0.1 & x5_pf < 0.95
  x5_za <- qnorm(0.975)
  x5_infl <- ((x5_za + qnorm(x5_pg[x5_ok])) /
                (x5_za + qnorm(x5_pf[x5_ok])))^2
  ## The lowest-power cell (both near 0.15) can fall just below 1
  ## within Monte Carlo error; the text names it.
  x5_lo <- which.min(x5_pg[x5_ok])
  stopifnot(all(x5_ok), all(x5_infl > 0.9),
            all(x5_infl[-x5_lo] > 1), x5_lo == 1)
  x5_hi <- x5_infl[-x5_lo]
  ## Text: G10 is liberal under the constant natural-history and
  ## placebo pathways and inside the band under the other two.
  stopifnot(x5_prog[['prog-TV-const']] > ss_band1[2],
            x5_prog[['prog-PB']] > ss_band1[2],
            x5_prog[['prog-TV-grow']] <= ss_band1[2],
            x5_prog[['prog-BL']] <= ss_band1[2])
}
x5_txt <- function(v) p01_pend(have_x5, ss_f(v))
```

**G10 under these pathways.** The planning sample sizes for G10
(paper 02) assume that the biomarker is not prognostic. We fitted G10 to the
trials of this stress test, with the baseline row. It rejected the
null at `r p01_pend(have_x5, ss_f(x5_r('curve-C07')))` in the base
cell, and at
`r x5_txt(x5_prog[['prog-TV-const']])`,
`r x5_txt(x5_prog[['prog-TV-grow']])`,
`r x5_txt(x5_prog[['prog-PB']])` and
`r x5_txt(x5_prog[['prog-BL']])` under the constant natural-history,
growing natural-history, placebo and baseline-severity pathways
(single-cell band `r ss_f(ss_band1[1])` to `r ss_f(ss_band1[2])`).
The expectancy-term model rejected
`r ss_f(min(ss_m3['F1', ]))` to `r ss_f(max(ss_m3['F1', ]))` in the
same cells. In this test G10 held its level when the biomarker acted
through baseline severity or the growing natural history, but not when
it acted through a constant natural history or the placebo response.
Section \@ref(sec-reconcile) shows why the growing case may not carry
over to an analysis without a baseline row. A trial in which a
constant natural-history or placebo pathway is plausible should be
planned for the expectancy-term analysis. On the power-curve trials of
the stress test, matching G10's power with that analysis needs about
`r p01_pend(have_x5, sprintf('%.2f to %.2f', min(x5_hi), max(x5_hi)))`
times the G10 sample size, by the normal approximation to power, at
$c_{bm}$ from 0.225 to 0.45. At $c_{bm} = 0.15$ both analyses have
power near 0.15 and the factor,
`r p01_pend(have_x5, sprintf('%.2f', x5_infl[x5_lo]))`, is within
Monte Carlo error of 1. Paper 02's G10 sample sizes can be scaled by
that factor. The factor comes from one design, half-life and $\rho$,
the stress test's base cell.

```{r pooled-extra4}
## Pooled second run plus --extra4 (2,000 trials per cell), written by
## 15-extra4-pooled-inputs.R; power_adj is size-adjusted power.
pl_dat <- read.csv(file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'data', 'quick-sim',
  'carryover-closed-form', 'strawman-stress', 'extra4-decision',
  'pooled', 'decision-power-ds-nosym-all14-x.csv'))
pl_adj <- function(lab, cbm, an) {
  x <- pl_dat$power_adj[pl_dat$label == lab &
                        abs(pl_dat$cbm - cbm) < 1e-9 &
                        pl_dat$analysis == an]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1, pl_dat$n[pl_dat$label == lab &
    abs(pl_dat$cbm - cbm) < 1e-9 & pl_dat$analysis == an] == 2000)
  x
}
pl_f <- function(...) sprintf('%.3f', pl_adj(...))
```

**Power and robustness.** The expectancy-term model keeps its size
under every prognostic pathway and has lower power. In the base cell
at $c_{bm} = 0.30$ its power was
`r ss_f(ss_r(ss3, 'curve-C07', 'F1', 0.3))` against
`r ss_f(ss_r(ss3, 'curve-C07', 'S', 0.3))` for the CAR(1) model. A
further 1,500 trials per cell under the second run's DGP (randomized
allocation) were pooled with that run (2,000 per cell). There,
size-adjusted power was `r pl_f('curve-C07', 0.3, 'F1')` against
`r pl_f('curve-C07', 0.3, 'S')`, about
`r sprintf('%.0f', 100 * (1 - pl_adj('curve-C07', 0.3, 'F1') / pl_adj('curve-C07', 0.3, 'S')))`%
less. Under compound symmetry at $c_{bm} = 0.25$ the gap closes. Power
was `r ss_f(ss_r(ss3, 'curve-CS', 'F1', 0.25))` against
`r ss_f(ss_r(ss3, 'curve-CS', 'S', 0.25))` in the reported run, and
size-adjusted power in the pooled trials was
`r pl_f('curve-CS', 0.25, 'F1')` against
`r pl_f('curve-CS', 0.25, 'S')` (Monte Carlo SE about 0.011). The
choice between power and robustness is the trialist's. It depends on
whether a prognostic pathway absent at baseline is plausible for the
biomarker in hand.

### The growing pathway and the trend pathway {#sec-reconcile}

```{r values-reconcile, include = FALSE}
## Driver 11 stores estimates per unit of the raw biomarker (bmc is
## centered, not scaled); the paper 02 core stores them per SD. The
## biomarker SD is read from driver 11's source of constants.
rc_here04 <- file.path(repo_root, 'analysis', 'scripts', 'quick-sim',
                       'hendrickson-problems', '04-power-simulation.R')
rc_env <- new.env()
for (e in parse(rc_here04)) {
  if (is.call(e) && identical(e[[1]], as.name('<-')) &&
        is.name(e[[2]]) &&
        as.character(e[[2]]) %in% c('bm_sd', 'gomp', 'designs',
                                    'path_info')) {
    eval(e, rc_env)
  }
}
has_rc <- has_rvT && have_x5 &&
  all(c('bm_sd', 'gomp', 'designs', 'path_info') %in% ls(rc_env))
if (has_rc) {
  rc_bm_sd <- rc_env$bm_sd
  bpT <- rvT_m$params$baseline_param
  rpT <- rvT_m$params$resp_param
  claim(isTRUE(all.equal(rc_bm_sd, bpT$sd[bpT$cat == 'bm'],
                         tolerance = 1e-6)),
        'Driver 11 and block T use the same biomarker SD.')
  setv('rc_sig_tv', sprintf('%g', rpT$sd[rpT$cat == 'tv']))
  rc_main <- read.csv(file.path(ss_dir,
                                'summary-full-anchored-fixed-ha0.5.csv'))
  rc_get <- function(d, an) {
    x <- d[d$label == 'prog-TV-grow' & d$cbm == 0 & d$analysis == an, ]
    stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
    c(reject = x$reject, est = x$mean_est * rc_bm_sd,
      se = x$emp_sd * rc_bm_sd)
  }
  rc_S <- rc_get(rc_main, 'S')
  rc_DS <- rc_get(rc_main, 'DS')
  rc_F1 <- rc_get(rc_main, 'F1')
  rc_G10 <- rc_get(x5, 'G10')
  rc_T <- function(m) {
    x <- row1(rvT, method == m, c_bm == 0)
    c(reject = x$reject, est = x$mean_est, se = x$emp_se)
  }
  rc_G8 <- rc_T('E2cr2')
  rc_G9 <- rc_T('E7cr2')
  rc_TF <- rc_T('F1')
  for (nm in c('S', 'DS', 'F1', 'G10', 'G8', 'G9', 'TF')) {
    v <- get(paste0('rc_', nm))
    setv(paste0('rc_', nm, '_r'), f3(v[['reject']]))
    setv(paste0('rc_', nm, '_e'), fs2(v[['est']]))
    setv(paste0('rc_', nm, '_s'), f2(v[['se']]))
  }
  claim(sign(rc_S[['est']]) == -sign(rc_G8[['est']]),
        paste('Growing shift: the fixed-half-life estimate has opposite',
              'signs with and without the baseline row.'))
  claim(all(abs(c(rc_S[['est']], rc_DS[['est']], rc_G10[['est']],
                  rc_G8[['est']], rc_G9[['est']])) <
              c(rc_S[['se']], rc_DS[['se']], rc_G10[['se']],
                rc_G8[['se']], rc_G9[['se']]) / 3),
        paste('Growing shift: every G-type mean estimate is within a',
              'third of its empirical SE of zero.'))
  claim(in_band(rc_S[['reject']], 1000) &&
          in_band(rc_G8[['reject']], 1000) &&
          in_band(rc_G10[['reject']], 1000) &&
          in_band(rc_DS[['reject']], 1000),
        paste('Growing shift: G8, the CAR(1) model, its AIC variant',
              'and G10 are inside the band.'))
  ## Least-squares projection of the shift onto the biomarker terms
  ## of Sx ~ bm + t + Dbc + bm:Dbc at the true half-life, with no
  ## covariance weighting: the Dbc coefficient of the shift on
  ## [1, Dbc], pooled over the four Hybrid paths with equal weight.
  ## A sign check of the mechanism, not a prediction of the estimate.
  rc_D <- rc_env$designs$Hybrid
  rc_pi <- lapply(rc_D$paths, function(od) {
    rc_env$path_info(rc_D$t_wk, rc_D$e, od)
  })
  rc_g <- rc_env$gomp(rc_pi[[1]]$w, 6.50647, 5, 0.35)
  rc_g <- rc_g / max(rc_g)
  rc_dbc <- unlist(lapply(rc_pi, function(p) {
    ifelse(p$on, 1, ifelse(p$tsd > 0, 0.5^(p$tsd / 0.5), 0))
  }))
  rc_shift <- -0.3 * rpT$sd[rpT$cat == 'tv'] *
    rep(rc_g, length(rc_pi))
  rc_ols0 <- coef(lm(rc_shift ~ rc_dbc))[[2]]
  rc_dbc1 <- c(rc_dbc, rep(0, length(rc_pi)))
  rc_shift1 <- c(rc_shift, rep(0, length(rc_pi)))
  rc_ols1 <- coef(lm(rc_shift1 ~ rc_dbc1))[[2]]
  rc_z <- vapply(list(rc_S, rc_DS, rc_G10, rc_G8, rc_G9), function(v) {
    abs(v[['est']]) / (v[['se']] / sqrt(1000))
  }, numeric(1))
  setv('rc_zmin', sprintf('%.1f', min(rc_z)))
  claim(min(rc_z) > 2,
        paste('Growing shift: every G-type mean estimate is more than',
              'two Monte Carlo SEs from zero.'))
  setv('rc_ols0', fs2(rc_ols0))
  setv('rc_ols1', fs2(rc_ols1))
  claim(sign(rc_ols0) == sign(rc_G8[['est']]) &&
          sign(rc_ols1) == sign(rc_S[['est']]),
        paste('Growing shift: the unweighted projection has the sign',
              'of the estimate with and without the baseline row.'))
}
```

The growing natural-history pathway of this test and the trend
pathway of Section \@ref(sec-trend) are the same mean shift. Both add
$0.3\,\sigma_{TV}\,z_i\,g(w_t)$ to the natural-history component,
with $g$ the natural-history mean course scaled to peak 1 over the
visits. Driver 11 applies it in `draw()`. The paper 02 driver
applies it in `implementations/tidyverse/R/functions.R`. Both use the
published natural-history curve, $\sigma_{TV} =$ `r V('rc_sig_tv')`,
the Hybrid design with fixed allocation, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$
week and 1,000 null replicates. The two results appear to disagree.
Under the trend pathway G9 exceeded the band. Under the growing
pathway G10 stayed inside it.

The comparison is less direct than that. The two tests did not fit
the same analyses. Block T fitted G8, G9 and F1, not G10. The second
test fitted G10 but not G8 or G9. Its CAR(1) model with CR2 at the
fixed half-life of 0.5 week has the formula, covariance and test of
G8. Its AIC variant resembles G9, with a grid that adds 0. The two
tests also differ in their analysis data. Every analysis of the
second test has a baseline row. The paper 02 driver has none. Table
\@ref(tab:tab-reconcile) sets the comparable analyses side by side.
The comparison is across jobs and unpaired.

```{r tab-reconcile}
if (has_rc) {
  rc_cell <- function(k) {
    if (is.null(k)) return('--')
    sprintf('%s (%s; %s)', V(paste0('rc_', k, '_r')),
            V(paste0('rc_', k, '_e')), V(paste0('rc_', k, '_s')))
  }
  rc_tab <- data.frame(
    Analysis = c('Fixed half-life 0.5 week, CR2',
                 'Half-life by AIC, interaction in the model',
                 'Half-life by AIC, interaction not in the model',
                 'Expectancy terms, fixed half-life'),
    T = c(paste('G8:', rc_cell('G8')), paste('G9:', rc_cell('G9')),
          'not fitted', paste('F1 (0.2 week):', rc_cell('TF'))),
    S = c(paste('CAR(1):', rc_cell('S')),
          paste('AIC variant:', rc_cell('DS')),
          paste('G10:', rc_cell('G10')),
          paste('Expectancy-term (0.5 week):', rc_cell('F1'))))
  knitr::kable(rc_tab, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Analysis', 'Block T, no baseline row',
                  'Second stress test, baseline row'),
    caption = sprintf('The growing natural-history shift ($0.3\\,
      \\sigma_{TV}\\,z_i\\,g(w_t)$) with no true interaction, in the two
      drivers. Each entry: rejection rate (mean interaction estimate
      per SD of the biomarker; empirical SE). Hybrid, $N = 70$,
      $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, fixed allocation, 1,000 replicates. Band
      %s. The estimates of the second test are converted from raw
      biomarker units by its SD.', V('t_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 8) |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = '4cm') |>
    kableExtra::column_spec(2:3, width = '4.6cm')
} else {
  pending_note('the comparison of the growing and trend pathways')
}
```

At the fixed half-life the two drivers agree on size. G8 rejected at
`r V('rc_G8_r')` and the CAR(1) model at `r V('rc_S_r')`, both inside
the band. G9 rejected at `r V('rc_G9_r')`, above it, and the AIC
variant of the second test at `r V('rc_DS_r')`. The mean estimates
differ in sign. Without a baseline row G8 gave `r V('rc_G8_e')` per SD
of the biomarker. With one, the CAR(1) model gave `r V('rc_S_e')` and
G10 `r V('rc_G10_e')`. Every one of these is within a third of its
empirical SE of zero.

The baseline row accounts for the change of sign. The shift is zero
at week 0 and grows along the natural-history curve. In the Hybrid
design the off-drug visits come late, where the shift is large.
Without a baseline row the off-drug visits carry more of the shift
than the on-drug visits. The shift lowers the outcome, so the
difference projects onto $B^c_i D_{bc,it}$ with a positive sign. A
baseline row adds an off-drug row with no shift. That reverses the
sign. An unweighted least-squares projection of the shift onto the
biomarker terms of the G8 model gives `r V('rc_ols0')` per SD of the
biomarker without the baseline row and `r V('rc_ols1')` with it. It
ignores the random intercept and the CAR(1) weighting, so it checks
only the signs, which agree with the fitted estimates.

The two results therefore do not conflict. The DGP settings match.
The difference lies in the analysis data and in which analyses were
fitted. Two points remain open. First, G10 has not been fitted under
the trend pathway without a baseline row. That it held its level
under the growing pathway rests on analyses with a baseline row only.
Second, the bias is real in both tests. Every G-type mean estimate in
Table \@ref(tab:tab-reconcile) is at least `r V('rc_zmin')` Monte
Carlo SEs from zero. It is within a third of the empirical SE at
$N = 70$, so it moves the rejection rate little there. As under the
placebo-response pathway (Section \@ref(sec-largen)), a fixed bias of
either sign inflates the size of the two-sided test as $N$ grows. The
sign here depends on the visit structure of the analysis. A larger
sample under the trend pathway, with the same analysis fitted with
and without the baseline row, would settle both points. The biomarker-by-time block of Section
\@ref(sec-bmt) should include that contrast.

## The biomarker-by-time remedy: RESULTS PENDING {#sec-bmt}

\fbox{\parbox{0.95\linewidth}{\textbf{RESULTS PENDING.} The
simulation for this section has not been run. This section contains
no results. It will be written from the block described in the split
plan, Section 3.1, once that block is stored.}}

The remedy adds a biomarker-by-time term $B^c_i w_t$ to the analysis
model, as `bmc:t`. Its coefficient would be written
$\beta_{bm:T}$ (*proposed*). A quadratic variant adds $B^c_i w_t^2$.
The planned block crosses the trend pathway, present or absent, with
a null and an alternative interaction. It fits G8, G9, G10 and F1A0
with and without the term to the same trials. It answers three
questions. Does the term remove the trend bias in size and in the
mean estimate? What does it cost in power when there is no trend?
Does a linear term suffice when the natural-history course is not a
straight line? Section \@ref(sec-reconcile) adds a fourth: does the
answer depend on whether the analysis has a baseline row? The block
should fit each analysis both ways. The driver changes it needs are listed in the
Reproducibility section.

## Expectancy terms without a prognostic effect {#sec-gvf}

The F-family's cost when the biomarker is predictive only was
measured on the original 30-cell grid of paper 02 under the published
parameter set (`r V('g_n')` replicates per cell). The F-family is
not estimable under CO, so only the Hybrid and OL+BDC cells enter.
Table \@ref(tab:tab-gvf) gives the rejection rates.

```{r tab-gvf}
if (has_s27) {
  tv <- s27 |>
    filter(design != 'CO',
           method %in% c('E7cr2', 'E7null_cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0',
                         'F1A0B')) |>
    mutate(Method = m_lab[method],
           Design = ifelse(design == 'OLBDC', 'OL+BDC', design)) |>
    arrange(Design, c_bm, t1half, N) |>
    select(Design, c_bm, t1half, N, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    select(Design, c_bm, t1half, N, G9, G10, F1, F1A0, F1A0B) |>
    mutate(c_bm = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
           t1half = sprintf('%.1f', t1half),
           across(c(G9, G10, F1, F1A0, F1A0B), f3))
  tv$Design[duplicated(tv$Design)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(tv, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Design', '$c_{bm}$', '$t_{1/2}$', '$N$', 'G9',
                  'G10', 'F1', 'F1A0', 'F1A0B'),
    caption = sprintf('Original 30-cell grid of paper 02, published
      parameter set, Hybrid and OL+BDC cells: rejection rate with no
      prognostic effect. %s replicates per cell, the same trials for
      every analysis. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ are Type I error (band
      %s).', V('g_n'), V('g_band'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the published-set original grid')
}
```

The null rates were `r V('g_null_g10')` for G10, `r V('g_null_f1a0')`
for F1A0, `r V('g_null_fb')` for F1A0B and `r V('g_null_f1')` for F1.
Over the alternative cells of the Hybrid design, F1A0 reached
`r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0')` percent of the mean power of G10, F1A0B
`r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1A0B')` percent and F1 `r V('g_r_Hybrid_F1')`
percent. Under OL+BDC the figures were `r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1A0')`,
`r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1A0B')` and `r V('g_r_OLBDC_F1')` percent. The mean
paired difference from G10 over the `r V('g_k')` Hybrid alternative
cells was `r V('g_pd_Hybrid_F1A0')` for F1A0 (SE
`r V('g_pse_Hybrid_F1A0')`) and `r V('g_pd_Hybrid_F1')` for F1
(`r V('g_pse_Hybrid_F1')`). Under OL+BDC it was
`r V('g_pd_OLBDC_F1A0')` (`r V('g_pse_OLBDC_F1A0')`) and
`r V('g_pd_OLBDC_F1')` (`r V('g_pse_OLBDC_F1')`). The pooled
standard errors treat the cells as independent. Cells at the same
$N$ share random-number streams, so they are approximate.

F1 also loses power where its fixed half-life is wrong. In block A
at a true half-life of 2 weeks and $c_{bm} = 0.45$, F1 reached
`r V('a_f1_pw')` against `r V('a_g10_pw')` for G10. Its mean estimate
was `r V('a_f1_est')` against `r V('a_g10_est')` for G10 and a true
value of `r V('truth45')`. The fixed half-life is the cost, not the
expectancy terms. F1A0, which selects the half-life, is the fair
comparator for the terms themselves.

```{r tab-scen}

  sc_lab <- c(hybrid_null = 'Hybrid, null',

  tsc <- s21 |>
```

## The repair artifact: a historical exhibit {#sec-artifact}

\fbox{\parbox{0.95\linewidth}{\textbf{Historical exhibit.} Every
number in this section comes from runs under the simcore2026 parameter
set with silent repair (Table \ref{tab:tab-sources}). They are
evidence about a repaired DGP. They are not evidence about any
analysis under a prognostic biomarker.}}

The first prognostic stress test ran at strengths 0.3 and 0.6 before
the drivers refused infeasible matrices. At strength 0.6 on the
placebo-response and natural-history pathways, G9 lost
`r V('h_loss6')` points of power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ against the
no-confound reference of `r V('h_ref35')` ($N = 35$) and
`r V('h_ref70')` ($N = 70$). At strength 0.3 the largest loss was
`r V('h_loss3')`. Every one of the `r V('h_nmeth')` analyses fitted
to the same trials lost power at strength 0.6 (Table
\@ref(tab:tab-hist)). That uniformity was the first sign that the
loss arose before the analysis.

```{r tab-hist}
if (has_st_h) {
  th <- st_h |>
    filter(c_bm == 0.45, method %in% c('E7cr2', 'F1', 'F1A0B'),
           pathway != 'progtvgrow') |>
    mutate(Pathway = path_lab[pathway], Method = m_lab[method]) |>
    select(pathway, Pathway, N, strength, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(Method, strength), values_from = reject,
                names_sep = ' ') |>
    arrange(match(pathway, path_ord), N) |>
    select(Pathway, N, `G9 0.3`, `G9 0.6`, `F1 0.3`, `F1 0.6`,
           `F1A0B 0.3`, `F1A0B 0.6`) |>
    mutate(across(-c(Pathway, N), f3))
  th$Pathway[duplicated(th$Pathway)] <- ''
  knitr::kable(th, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    col.names = c('Pathway', '$N$', rep(c('0.3', '0.6'), 3)),
    caption = sprintf('Historical exhibit (simcore2026 parameter set,
      silent repair): power at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ at prognostic
      strengths 0.3 and 0.6, Hybrid, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, %s
      replicates. Every strength-0.6 cell here, including
      $c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$, was simulated under a repaired matrix.',
      fn(st_h_m$n_reps))) |>
    kableExtra::add_header_above(c(' ' = 2, 'G9' = 2, 'F1' = 2,
                                   'F1A0B' = 2)) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical prognostic stress test')
}
```

A direct check of the covariance matrices explains it (Table
\@ref(tab:tab-pd)). Each strength-0.6 cell on those two pathways, and
$c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$ at $c_{bm} = 0.45$, has a joint matrix that is not
positive definite on all `r V('h_npaths')` Hybrid paths. The repair
replaced it with a nearby matrix before any data were drawn. The
repair shrank the population on-drug minus off-drug slope of the
outcome on the biomarker. That is the quantity the interaction term
estimates. With no prognostic correlation it is `r V('h_c_none')`.
After repair it was `r V('h_c_pb6')` under the placebo-response
pathway and `r V('h_c_tv6')` under the natural-history pathway. The
power loss is the repair removing part of the interaction from the
data. No analysis could recover it. At strength 0.3 the matrix is
positive definite, with a smallest eigenvalue of `r V('h_eig_pb3')`
under the placebo-response pathway.

```{r tab-pd}
if (has_pdc) {
  tpd <- pdc$summary |>
    filter(pathway != 'progtvgrow',
           !(pathway == 'none' & c_bm == 0),
           c_bm == 0.45 | strength == 0.6) |>
    mutate(Pathway = ifelse(pathway == 'none', 'none',
                            path_lab[pathway])) |>
    transmute(Pathway, Strength = sprintf('%.1f', strength),
              `$c_{bm}$` = sprintf('%.2f', c_bm),
              `Paths repaired` = paths_repaired,
              `Min. eigenvalue` = f3(min_eigenvalue),
              `Contrast, raw` = fs2(contrast_raw),
              `Contrast, repaired` = fs2(contrast_repaired))
  knitr::kable(tpd, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = 'Historical exhibit: positive definiteness of the raw
      joint covariance matrix on the Hybrid paths, and the population
      on-drug minus off-drug slope of the outcome on the biomarker
      before and after the silent repair. Computed from the matrix
      under the simcore2026 SDs, no simulation
      (\\texttt{30-check-prognostic-confound-pd.R}).') |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical positive-definiteness check')
}
```

Before the artifact was found, the loss was read as patient-level
variance that a random intercept could not absorb. G9 was refitted
with a random slope on time, on expectancy, and on both, in
`r V('re_ncell')` cells at `r V('re_reps')` replicates. `r V('re_n6')`
of those cells are repaired strength-0.6 cells. The three variants
matched plain G9 to within `r V('re_dmax')` in rejection rate in every
cell (Table \@ref(tab:tab-re)). The largest paired per-replicate
difference was `r V('m12_dmax')`. Non-convergence reached
`r V('re_nonconv')` percent for the variant with both slopes. The DGP
has no patient-specific slope, so there was no variance for a random
slope to absorb. The check shows only that the slopes cost nothing
there.

```{r tab-re}
if (has_re_h) {
  re_lab <- c(G9 = 'G9', G9rs = '+ slope on $w_t$',
              G9re = '+ slope on $\\eta_t$', G9rse = '+ both')
  tre <- re_h |>
    mutate(Cell = sprintf('%s, $c_{bm} = %.2f$, $N = %d$',
                          ifelse(pathway == 'none', 'none',
                                 paste(path_lab[pathway], strength)),
                          c_bm, N),
           Method = re_lab[method]) |>
    select(Cell, Method, reject) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Method, values_from = reject) |>
    mutate(across(-Cell, f3))
  knitr::kable(tre, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
    caption = sprintf('Historical exhibit: rejection rate of G9 and
      its three random-slope variants (simcore2026 parameter set,
      Hybrid, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week, %s replicates). The strength-0.6
      rows were simulated under repaired matrices.', V('re_reps'))) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
} else {
  pending_note('the historical random-slope runs')
}
```

The published-set rerun applied the current default, which refuses an
infeasible matrix. Of its `r V('n6_cells')` strength-0.6 cells on the
three correlation pathways, `r V('n6_refused')` were refused and
`r V('n6_ran')` ran. The refused cells are exactly the configurations
that the historical check found infeasible. The cells that ran set
$c_{bm,BL} = 0.6$ with no true interaction, which is feasible. Under
the current code a repaired cell cannot be simulated without an
explicit option.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

## What the expectancy terms are for {#sec-expectancy}

The placebo-response amplitude scales with $\eta_t$. In the Hybrid
design $\eta_t$ differs between on-drug and off-drug visits. A
biomarker correlated with the placebo response therefore acquires an
on/off slope difference with no true interaction. Under the
simcore2026 SDs the population contrast was `r V('h_c_pb3n')` at
$c_{bm,PB} = 0.3$ and `r V('h_c_pb6n')` at 0.6, against
`r V('h_c_none')` for the interaction at $c_{bm} = 0.45$ (historical,
Table \@ref(tab:tab-pd)). The placebo-response SD is
`r V('sig_pb_sc')` in the simcore2026 set and `r V('sig_pb')` in the
published set. The contrast scales with that SD. It has not been
recomputed under the published set.

The published-set runs show the consequence. Under the
placebo-response pathway the G-family estimate moved away from zero
with no interaction present (Section \@ref(sec-grid)). The bias was
small against the standard error at $N = 70$ and produced no excess
rejection there. At $N = 280$ it did (Section \@ref(sec-largen)).
The F-family, whose $B^c_i\eta_t$ term absorbs the contrast, stayed
inside the band at every $N$ examined. The earlier conclusion that
the expectancy terms add nothing came from the simcore2026 runs. It
does not hold under the published parameter values.

## Whether the analysis has a baseline row {#sec-baselinerow}

The results come from two kinds of analysis data. The paper 02
driver starts at the first post-baseline visit. The second stress test
adds baseline as an off-drug row. The choice changes how a prognostic
pathway reaches the interaction term. Without a baseline row, the
correlation pathways at strength 0.3 left G9 and G10 inside the band
at $N \le 70$ (Section \@ref(sec-stress)), and the placebo-response
bias became visible only at $N = 280$ (Section \@ref(sec-largen)).
With a baseline row, a pathway absent at baseline also enters through
the single biomarker main effect shared by baseline and the off-drug
visits (Appendix \@ref(sec-shared)). G10 then exceeded the band at
$N = 70$ under the natural-history and placebo-response correlations
(Section \@ref(sec-tenan)). Under the trend pathway the baseline row
reversed the sign of the bias (Section \@ref(sec-reconcile)). The
expectancy-term analyses kept their size in both kinds of data. Which
convention a trial's analysis follows is therefore part of its
specification. A study that plans G10 for a biomarker that may be
prognostic should state it.

## The joint recommendation {#sec-recommend}

This paper and paper 02 give one recommendation between them.

- For a biomarker believed to be predictive only, use G10: the
  exposure-weighted indicator with the half-life chosen by AIC on the
  model without the interaction, tested with CR2
  [@pmsimstats-paper02].
- Where the biomarker may also be prognostic, add the
  design-expectancy terms $\eta_t$ and $B^c_i\eta_t$. This is F1A0,
  or its bootstrap-calibrated form F1A0B. F1A0 and G10 differ only in
  those two terms.
- Where the biomarker may predict the rate of natural-history change,
  also add a biomarker-by-time term. This step is provisional until
  the block of Section \@ref(sec-bmt) is run.

F1, which fixes the half-life at 0.2 week, is not recommended. It
loses power wherever that value is wrong (Section \@ref(sec-gvf)).
Two questions remain for F1A0B. Its bootstrap calibration may be
unnecessary once the selection excludes the interaction. Its cost
against G10 without a prognostic effect is measured here on one grid
only.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

The published-set results come from one parameter set and one
correlation structure ($\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$). Most cells are on
the Hybrid design at $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week. The prognostic correlations
are correlations of a single latent biomarker with the components.
The feasibility bound is a property of that parameterization. The
large-sample cells have no confound-free counterpart at the same $N$.
The trend pathway was simulated at one coefficient, one sample size
and one half-life. The sign of its bias depends on whether the
analysis has a baseline row, and no single job has fitted the same
analysis both ways. G10 has not been fitted under it without a
baseline row. Its remedy has not been simulated. The second stress
test ran 1,000 null replicates per cell at one sample size, and its
cells and analyses were revised as results came in. The
placebo-response contrast has not been recomputed under the published
SDs. The random-slope variants were fitted only to historical,
partly repaired cells under a DGP without patient-specific slopes.
Comparisons with the block A reference are across jobs and unpaired.
Cells within a job share random-number streams, so counts of cells
inside a band are not independent confirmations.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. A constant prognostic shift is absorbed exactly by the biomarker
   main effect. It cannot move the interaction estimate.
2. Inside the feasibility bounds, and without a baseline row, the
   correlation pathways left the G9 and G10 Type I error inside the
   band at $N \le 70$.
3. A biomarker correlated with the placebo response biases the
   G-family estimate. Under the published parameter values the bias
   inflated the size of G9 and G10 at $N = 280$. The expectancy terms
   removed it.
4. A biomarker that predicts the natural-history trend biased every
   analysis fitted by the paper 02 driver, which has no baseline row.
   The expectancy terms absorbed part of the bias. With a baseline
   row the bias changed sign. At $N = 70$ the mean estimate was
   within a third of its empirical SE of zero in both. The
   biomarker-by-time remedy is pending.
5. In the second stress test, whose analyses have a baseline row, the
   expectancy-term analyses kept their size under all four pathways.
   G10 exceeded the band under the constant natural-history and
   placebo-response pathways.
6. The power loss once attributed to a prognostic correlation of 0.6
   was produced by the silent repair of infeasible matrices. Under the
   current default those cells are refused.
7. For a biomarker that may be prognostic, add $\eta_t$ and
   $B^c_i\eta_t$ to G10. The result is F1A0.

# (APPENDIX) Appendix {-}

# Absorption of a constant shift {#sec-absorb}

Let $X$ be the fixed-effects design matrix of any analysis here. It
contains the biomarker main effect $B^c_i$. The constant shift adds
$b_{TV}\sigma_{TV} z_i$ to every outcome of participant $i$. Since
$z_i$ is an affine function of $B^c_i$, the shift vector lies in the
column space of $X$. For fixed variance parameters the generalized
least-squares estimate then changes only in the coefficients of the
intercept and $B^c_i$. The residuals are unchanged. REML and ML
estimates of the variance parameters depend on the data only through
those residuals, so they are unchanged too. AIC selection compares
fits whose likelihoods are unchanged, so it selects the same
half-life. CR2 standard errors depend on the residuals and the design
only. The interaction estimate, its standard error and its $p$-value
are therefore identical, replicate by replicate. The stored data
confirm it (Section \@ref(sec-stress)).

# The joint feasibility condition {#sec-jointfeas}

Order the variables as biomarker, then everything else, and let $M_0$
be the correlation matrix of everything but the biomarker, including
the baseline level, which is uncorrelated with the response
components. By the Schur complement the joint matrix is positive
definite if and only if $M_0$ is and the biomarker row $r$ satisfies
$r^\top M_0^{-1} r < 1$. With $c_{bm}$ alone, $r = c_{bm}\tilde g$,
where $\tilde g$ is the correlation profile padded with zeros, and the
bound is $c_{bm}^{\ast} = (\tilde g^\top M_0^{-1}\tilde g)^{-1/2}$
[@pmsimstats-paper01].

With prognostic correlations the row is a sum of fixed patterns scaled
by the correlations,
$r = c_{bm}\tilde g + c_{bm,PB}\, p + c_{bm,TV}\, q + c_{bm,BL}\, b$.
Here $p$ and $q$ are one on every visit of the placebo-response and
natural-history components, and $b$ is one on the baseline level. The
condition becomes $c^\top A c < 1$, with
$c = (c_{bm}, c_{bm,PB}, c_{bm,TV}, c_{bm,BL})$ and
$A_{jk} = x_j^\top M_0^{-1} x_k$ for $x \in \{\tilde g, p, q, b\}$. The
feasible region is the interior of an ellipsoid. Fixing all
correlations but one makes $c^\top A c = 1$ a quadratic in that
correlation, whose positive root is its bound. A negative discriminant
means the fixed correlations are already infeasible. Because $b$ is an
eigenvector of $M_0$ with unit eigenvalue, $c_{bm,BL}$ enters only
through its square. Its bound given $c_{bm}$ is
$\sqrt{1 - c_{bm}^2 A_{\tilde g\tilde g}}$. The $p$ and $q$ patterns
are structurally identical, so $c_{bm,PB}$ and $c_{bm,TV}$ have the
same bounds. A design's bound is the minimum over its paths. Table
\@ref(tab:tab-jointceil) gives the values for the Hybrid design. The
off-diagonal entries of $A$ are negative at the extended DGP's values,
so the correlations are mildly complementary. The DGP sets the
biomarker's marginal correlations with the other components to zero.
The negative entries of $A$ reflect partial association: given its
correlation with the drug response, the biomarker's partial
correlation with the other components is not zero. An explicit
correlation of the same sign therefore uses less of the feasible
region than it would if the components were independent.

# The shared biomarker effect {#sec-shared}

Let $s_0$, $s_{\text{off}}$ and $s_{\text{on}}$ be the true slopes of
$Y$ on $B$ at baseline, at post-baseline off-drug visits and at
on-drug visits. A model with baseline as an off-drug row estimates one
$\beta_B$ for $s_0$ and $s_{\text{off}}$.

The following account is heuristic, not a derivation. Consider a
prognostic biomarker with no interaction, whose post-baseline slope is
constant: $s_0 = 0 \ne s_{\text{off}} = s_{\text{on}} = s_{\text{prog}}$.

- **The bias.** The fitted $\hat\beta_B$ lies between the baseline and
  off-drug slopes, $\hat\beta_B \approx f\,s_{\text{prog}}$ for some
  $0 < f < 1$ that depends on the weight the baseline row receives.
  The interaction absorbs the remainder,
  $\hat\beta_{bm:D} \approx (1 - f)\,s_{\text{prog}} \ne 0$.
- **The correction.** Adding $B_i\cdot\mathbf 1\{t = 0\}$ frees $s_0$
  and removes this source of bias. The constraint is analogous to the
  choice, in longitudinal analysis, between treating baseline as a
  covariate and as a response [@liu2009baseline].

Two further mechanisms operate in the scenarios of Section
\@ref(sec-tenan).

- **The slope grows over time.** When the post-baseline slope grows,
  the bias depends on how drug status is confounded with time.
  Freeing $s_0$ is then not sufficient in general. The rejection rate
  of `r ss_f(ss_m3['ES', 'prog-TV-grow'])` for that analysis under the
  growing pathway is consistent with this. Section
  \@ref(sec-reconcile) shows that the same growing shift biases the
  interaction with or without a baseline row, in opposite directions.
- **Expectancy.** When the biomarker is associated with the placebo
  response, the slope also scales with the expectancy $\eta_t$, which
  is higher at the open-label (on-drug) visits. The expectancy term
  $B_i \cdot \eta_t$, with $\eta_0 = 0$, addresses both this mechanism
  and the baseline constraint. Freeing $s_0$ alone does not. An
  expectancy-scaled slope still enters the interaction through the
  open-label visits.

Neither correction is exact in the Hybrid design. The expectancy term
removes a constant post-baseline slope from the interaction only when
the blinded on-drug and off-drug visits carry equal total weight. In
the Hybrid design they do not, so a small bias remains. The
corresponding derivations are in the project's compendium of
mathematical results (`analysis/report/compendium-mathematics.tex`).
The null rejection rates of Section \@ref(sec-tenan) across the four
prognostic cells were `r ss_f(min(ss_m3['F1', ]))` to
`r ss_f(max(ss_m3['F1', ]))` for the expectancy-term model and
`r ss_f(min(ss_m3['ES', ]))` to `r ss_f(max(ss_m3['ES', ]))` for the
free-baseline model. The residual bias of the expectancy-term model is
therefore within Monte Carlo error at the prognostic correlations
simulated. That of the free-baseline model is not, under the growing
pathway. Under a prognostic association with baseline severity alone
the binary-indicator analysis rejected
`r ss_f(ss_m3['R', 'prog-BL'])`, and the two corrections rejected
`r ss_f(ss_m3['F1', 'prog-BL'])` and `r ss_f(ss_m3['ES', 'prog-BL'])`.

# First run of the second stress test {#sec-firstrun}

The first run of the stress test of Section \@ref(sec-tenan) used the
compounding carryover rule on the mean and fixed path allocation (18,
18, 17, 17). Its table is given here for comparison with Table
\@ref(tab:tab-tenan). The two runs differ only in the carryover rule.

```{r tab-tenan-first}
ss_tab1 <- data.frame(Analysis = unname(ss_an), ss_bold(ss_m1),
                      check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ss_tab1, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE, linesep = '',
  col.names = c('Analysis', 'Natural history, constant',
                'Natural history, growing', 'Placebo response',
                'Baseline severity'),
  caption = 'Second stress test, first run (compounding carryover
    rule, fixed allocation): null rejection rates under a prognostic
    biomarker, 1,000 replicates per cell (two-MCSE band 0.036 to
    0.064 for a single cell). Rates above 0.075 in bold.') |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(1, width = '5.5cm') |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(2:5, width = '2.1cm')
```

# Draft consistency checks {#sec-checks}

```{r checks, results = 'asis'}
cat(sprintf('The prose of this draft makes %d qualitative statements
that are checked against the stored data when it renders. ',
            claim_env$n))
if (length(claim_env$fail) == 0) {
  cat('All of them hold.\n')
} else {
  cat(sprintf('%d do not hold and must be revised:\n\n',
              length(claim_env$fail)))
  cat(paste0('- ', claim_env$fail, collapse = '\n'), '\n')
}
```
